input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# deploy-cobra.sh — load & run the read-only rca-agent 0.3.0 on the Cobra jumpserver.
#
# This script is intended to run ON the Cobra jumpserver (s7427-Cobra-JS, 10.242.70.7)
# as user eagamil (uid/gid 1744, member of the docker group), after you have run
# `oc login` so that ~/.kube/config holds a valid token kubeconfig.
#
# It is READ-ONLY by construction: the agent only ever does get/list/watch against
# the cluster. It never mutates anything.
#
# Usage:
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh                 # verify checksum, load image, (re)start container, tail logs
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh --no-logs       # same but do not tail logs at the end
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh --skip-verify   # skip sha256 verification (not recommended)
#
# Override any default via environment variable, e.g.:
#   RCA_NAMESPACE=some-other-ns RCA_PORT=8005 ./deploy-cobra.sh
#   RCA_NF_SELECTOR='app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter' ./deploy-cobra.sh
#
set -euo pipefail

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration (override via environment)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
IMAGE_NAME="${IMAGE_NAME:-rca-agent}"
IMAGE_TAG="${IMAGE_TAG:-0.3.0}"
IMAGE_REF="${IMAGE_NAME}:${IMAGE_TAG}"

CONTAINER_NAME="${CONTAINER_NAME:-rca-agent}"

# Default target matches Cobra 2a / cSAEGW-C.
RCA_NAMESPACE="${RCA_NAMESPACE:-plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301}"
RCA_PORT="${RCA_PORT:-8004}"
# Empty selector = whole namespace. Narrow to one component to shrink the graph,
# e.g. RCA_NF_SELECTOR='app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter'
RCA_NF_SELECTOR="${RCA_NF_SELECTOR:-}"
RCA_REASONING_MODE="${RCA_REASONING_MODE:-extractive}"

# The uid:gid the container runs as. Must match the owner of ~/.kube/config
# (mode 600) so the mounted kubeconfig is readable. On Cobra that is 1744:1744.
RUN_UID_GID="${RUN_UID_GID:-1744:1744}"

# Path to the kubeconfig written by `oc login` on the jumpserver.
KUBECONFIG_HOST="${KUBECONFIG_HOST:-$HOME/.kube/config}"

# Artifacts shipped alongside this script.
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
IMAGE_TARBALL="${IMAGE_TARBALL:-$SCRIPT_DIR/rca-agent-${IMAGE_TAG}.tar.gz}"
SHA_FILE="${SHA_FILE:-${IMAGE_TARBALL}.sha256}"

SKIP_VERIFY=0
TAIL_LOGS=1
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --skip-verify) SKIP_VERIFY=1 ;;
    --no-logs)     TAIL_LOGS=0 ;;
    -h|--help)
      grep '^#' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "WARN: unknown arg '$arg' (ignored)" >&2 ;;
  esac
done

log()  { printf '\033[1;34m[deploy]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[error]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { err "$*"; exit 1; }

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pre-flight checks
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "docker not found on PATH."
docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "cannot talk to the docker daemon (is '$USER' in the docker group?)."

[ -f "$IMAGE_TARBALL" ] || die "image tarball not found: $IMAGE_TARBALL"

if [ ! -f "$KUBECONFIG_HOST" ]; then
  die "kubeconfig not found at $KUBECONFIG_HOST. Run 'oc login <api-url> -u <user> -p <pass> --insecure-skip-tls-verify' first."
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Verify checksum
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$SKIP_VERIFY" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ -f "$SHA_FILE" ]; then
    log "verifying sha256 of $(basename "$IMAGE_TARBALL") ..."
    ( cd "$(dirname "$IMAGE_TARBALL")" && sha256sum -c "$(basename "$SHA_FILE")" ) \
      || die "checksum verification FAILED — tarball is corrupt or truncated. Re-copy it."
    log "checksum OK."
  else
    err "no .sha256 sidecar found ($SHA_FILE); skipping verification."
  fi
else
  log "checksum verification skipped (--skip-verify)."
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load the image
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "loading image $IMAGE_REF from $(basename "$IMAGE_TARBALL") ..."
docker load -i "$IMAGE_TARBALL"
docker image inspect "$IMAGE_REF" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || die "image $IMAGE_REF not present after load (tarball tag mismatch?)."

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. (Re)start the container
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "removing any existing container named '$CONTAINER_NAME' ..."
docker rm -f "$CONTAINER_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

log "starting $CONTAINER_NAME (ns=$RCA_NAMESPACE port=$RCA_PORT user=$RUN_UID_GID selector='${RCA_NF_SELECTOR:-<whole-namespace>}') ..."
# NOTES on the flags (learned from earlier sessions):
#   --network host  : so the OpenShift API server URL resolves/reaches from inside.
#   --user 1744:1744: so the mounted (mode 600) kubeconfig is readable by the process.
#   -e HOME=/tmp    : uid 1744 has no /etc/passwd home inside the image; give it a writable one.
#   -v ...:ro       : kubeconfig mounted read-only.
docker run -d \
  --name "$CONTAINER_NAME" \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --network host \
  --user "$RUN_UID_GID" \
  -e RCA_CLUSTER_ENABLED=true \
  -e RCA_KUBECONFIG_MODE=local \
  -e RCA_NAMESPACE="$RCA_NAMESPACE" \
  -e RCA_NF_SELECTOR="$RCA_NF_SELECTOR" \
  -e RCA_REASONING_MODE="$RCA_REASONING_MODE" \
  -e RCA_PORT="$RCA_PORT" \
  -e KUBECONFIG=/kube/config \
  -e HOME=/tmp \
  -v "$KUBECONFIG_HOST":/kube/config:ro \
  "$IMAGE_REF"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Health check
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "waiting for the agent to answer /healthz on port $RCA_PORT ..."
ok=0
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do
  if curl -fsS "http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/healthz" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok=1; break
  fi
  sleep 1
done

if [ "$ok" -eq 1 ]; then
  log "healthy: $(curl -fsS "http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/healthz")"
  log "stats:   $(curl -fsS "http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/stats" || echo '(not ready yet — first cluster build may take ~a minute)')"
  cat <<EOF

  ✅ rca-agent ${IMAGE_TAG} is running.

  View from your LAPTOP via an SSH tunnel:
      ssh -L ${RCA_PORT}:localhost:${RCA_PORT} eagamil@10.242.70.7
  then open:
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/view                 (full graph; orphans hidden)
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/components            (components grouped by app.kubernetes.io/name)
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/view/component/<name> (one component's subgraph)
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/view/<pod>?radius=2   (neighborhood of a pod)
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/stats
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/docs                        (OpenAPI)

  Manage:
      docker logs -f ${CONTAINER_NAME}
      docker rm -f ${CONTAINER_NAME}
EOF
else
  err "agent did not become healthy on port ${RCA_PORT}. Recent logs:"
  docker logs --tail 40 "$CONTAINER_NAME" || true
  die "startup health check failed."
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Tail logs (optional)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$TAIL_LOGS" -eq 1 ]; then
  log "tailing logs (Ctrl-C to detach; container keeps running) ..."
  docker logs -f "$CONTAINER_NAME"
fi

Proven. The `skipping nodes: cannot list (403 Forbidden)` line is emitted (stderr), and the build still completes with a non-empty graph (10 nodes, 8 edges). The 403 on cluster-scoped `nodes` is **non-fatal** in 0.3.0 — identical behavior to 0.2.0.

So the `403 nodes` warning is a red herring. It is not the failure. Either:
1. The agent is actually fine and your log just ended at that warning (most likely), or
2. Something *else* after it broke — which the truncated log doesn't show.

To settle this definitively, I need the rest of your jumpserver output. Please run on the jumpserver:

```bash
docker logs rca-agent 2>&1 | tail -40
curl -s localhost:8004/graph/stats; echo
curl -s localhost:8004/healthz; echo
```

Here's how to read the result:

- If you see `graph rebuilt from cluster ns=plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 ... {'nodes': 1485, ...}` and `Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8004`, and `/graph/stats` returns a non-zero node count — **0.3.0 is working**. The 403 line is the same harmless cluster-nodes skip you also had on 0.2.0. Open `http://localhost:8004/graph/view` or the new `http://localhost:8004/graph/components` through your SSH tunnel.

- If instead you see a **Python traceback** after the 403 line, or `/graph/stats` returns `{"nodes":0,...}` while 0.2.0 returned 1485 — then there's a genuine 0.3.0 regression in a code path my local fake doesn't cover (most likely something touching a field on the real objects). Paste the traceback / the stats output and I'll pinpoint and fix it, rebuild the 0.3.0 tarball, and hand you the updated package.

My current evidence (34 tests pass, local 403-on-nodes build completes non-empty, local 0.3.0 container serves `/healthz`=0.3.0 and `/graph/stats`=11 nodes) says 0.3.0 is healthy. I just can't confirm the *real-cluster* run without those two command outputs from your jumpserver. What do they show?

Done. Here's what happened and what you now have.

## What was actually wrong

The `403 Forbidden` / `skipping daemonsets` lines were a red herring — those are expected and harmless (your `eagamil` token is namespace-scoped, so cluster-scoped types 403, and the code skips them). I proved this two ways: a diff showed `builder.py`, `kube_client.py`, and `dependency_graph.py` are **byte-identical** between 0.2.0 and 0.3.0, and a local 403-on-nodes build still produced a non-empty graph.

The real blocker, confirmed by your `docker ps` (Up) + `curl exit=7` (connection refused): **0.3.0 built the entire 1485-object graph synchronously at startup**, so uvicorn never bound its socket. The process was alive but not listening, and the log stalled mid-build. This was latent in 0.2.0 too; it just surfaced now.

## The fix (shipped as 0.3.1)

1. **Non-blocking startup** — the first graph build now runs in a background thread. `/healthz` answers in 0.03s while the build runs (verified). The logs now show `Application startup complete` and `Uvicorn running` *before* `initial graph built`.
2. **Bounded list calls** — every `list_*` is paginated server-side (`limit=500` + `_continue`) with a per-request timeout `(5s, 30s)`, so a big namespace can't hang.

Verified: 38 tests pass (added 4 regression tests), ruff clean, image smoke-tested.

## Your Cobra deployment package

`dist/cobra-package-0.3.1/` (tarball also at `/home/milind/rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz`):
- `rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz` — image, sha256 `22e182b11642dcaf42ee089c6f3be0c9a7d4e9a1ba158f520d750ca0613d6b94`
- `rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz.sha256`
- `deploy-cobra.sh` — verify + load + run + health-check (tested end-to-end locally)
- `DEPLOY-STEPS.md` — full steps + troubleshooting

## Deployment steps (short form)

```bash
# 1. laptop -> jumpserver
scp dist/cobra-package-0.3.1/* eagamil@10.242.70.7:~/

# 2. jumpserver: login + deploy
ssh eagamil@10.242.70.7
oc login https://api.cobra-2a-openshift.bete.ericy.com:6443 -u eagamil -p <pass> --insecure-skip-tls-verify
chmod +x deploy-cobra.sh && ./deploy-cobra.sh

# 3. laptop: tunnel + view
ssh -L 8004:localhost:8004 eagamil@10.242.70.7
#   http://localhost:8004/graph/view   (and /graph/stats, /graph/pods, /docs)
```

On the jumpserver you currently have the broken 0.3.0 running — the script will `docker rm -f` it and load 0.3.1. This time `/healthz` will answer immediately and `/graph/stats` node count will climb to ~1485 over the next minute. Full details and troubleshooting are in `DEPLOY-STEPS.md`.

[STEERING steer-01b30ae7108743daa9995125f55d0d7e: The `curl exit=7` (connection refused) was the decisive evidence that nothing was listening on 8004 despite the container being Up — confirming uvicorn hadn't bound because the synchronous startup build was still running. This validated the root cause and the non-blocking-startup fix I then implemented.]

No problem — you don't need the script. Since the 0.3.1 image tarball is also what you need there, here are the plain commands. You already have 0.3.0 running on the jumpserver; these replace it with the fixed 0.3.1.

## Step 1 — copy the new image tarball to the jumpserver (from your laptop/build host)

```bash
scp /home/milind/rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz eagamil@10.242.70.7:~/
```

(Optionally also copy the checksum: `scp /home/milind/telco-k8s-rca-agent/dist/cobra-package-0.3.1/rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz.sha256 eagamil@10.242.70.7:~/`)

## Step 2 — on the jumpserver: load and run 0.3.1

```bash
# (optional) verify the copy wasn't truncated
sha256sum rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz
# expect: 22e182b11642dcaf42ee089c6f3be0c9a7d4e9a1ba158f520d750ca0613d6b94

docker rm -f rca-agent
docker load -i ~/rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz
```

Then the run command **as a single line** (multi-line pastes get corrupted over SSH):

```bash
docker run -d --name rca-agent --restart unless-stopped --network host --user 1744:1744 -e RCA_CLUSTER_ENABLED=true -e RCA_KUBECONFIG_MODE=local -e RCA_NAMESPACE=plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 -e KUBECONFIG=/kube/config -e RCA_PORT=8004 -e HOME=/tmp -v ~/.kube/config:/kube/config:ro rca-agent:0.3.1
```

## Step 3 — confirm it's serving (this is the part that failed on 0.3.0)

```bash
docker logs -f rca-agent
curl -s localhost:8004/healthz   # expect: {"status":"ok","version":"0.3.1"}
curl -s localhost:8004/graph/stats
```

You should now see, in order:
```
rca-agent starting: ... (initial graph build running in background)
Application startup complete.
Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8004
skipping nodes: cannot list (403 Forbidden)      <- harmless
rca-agent initial graph built: {'nodes': 1485, ...}
```

`/healthz` answers **immediately** now; `/graph/stats` node count climbs from 0 to ~1485 over ~a minute as the background build runs.

## Step 4 — view from your laptop

```bash
ssh -L 8004:localhost:8004 eagamil@10.242.70.7
```
Then open `http://localhost:8004/graph/view` (also `/graph/stats`, `/graph/pods`, `/docs`).

Note: `oc login` must have been run already so `~/.kube/config` has a valid token. If you want to scope to one component instead of all 1485 nodes, add `-e RCA_NF_SELECTOR=app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter` to the `docker run` line.

If you'd rather have the script there after all, just `scp /home/milind/telco-k8s-rca-agent/dist/cobra-package-0.3.1/deploy-cobra.sh eagamil@10.242.70.7:~/` — but the four steps above do exactly what it does.

Two things stand out, and both are good news for the fix:

1. **The 0.3.1 fix works** — startup completed and uvicorn is serving (`/healthz` is up), and the build failure was caught and retried in the background instead of hanging. That's exactly the new behavior.
2. **This is a different, environmental problem**: `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/kube/config'`. The container (running as uid 1744) can't read the mounted kubeconfig.

Notice the prompt: `milind@E-5CG2310LQ9` — you ran this on the **build host**, not the Cobra jumpserver (`eagamil@s7427-Cobra-JS`). On the build host, `~/.kube/config` belongs to `milind` (uid 1000), but the container runs as `--user 1744:1744`, so uid 1744 is denied. The `--user 1744:1744` value only matches the *jumpserver's* `eagamil`.

Also, even if the permission were fixed, `~/.kube/config` on the build host likely doesn't point at Cobra 2a (no `oc login` there), so the build would still fail.

You have two clean options:

## Option A — run on the jumpserver (where it actually belongs)

That's where `eagamil` is uid 1744 and where `oc login` has written a valid Cobra token. Copy the tarball there and run it as before:

```bash
scp /home/milind/rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz eagamil@10.242.70.7:~/
ssh eagamil@10.242.70.7
oc login https://api.cobra-2a-openshift.bete.ericy.com:6443 -u eagamil -p <pass> --insecure-skip-tls-verify
docker rm -f rca-agent
docker load -i ~/rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz
docker run -d --name rca-agent --restart unless-stopped --network host --user 1744:1744 -e RCA_CLUSTER_ENABLED=true -e RCA_KUBECONFIG_MODE=local -e RCA_NAMESPACE=plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 -e KUBECONFIG=/kube/config -e RCA_PORT=8004 -e HOME=/tmp -v ~/.kube/config:/kube/config:ro rca-agent:0.3.1
```

## Option B — run on the build host (E-5CG2310LQ9) for a quick local test

If you deliberately want to test on the build host, fix the two mismatches:

1. Run the container as **your** uid so it can read your kubeconfig. Drop `--user 1744:1744` (use `--user $(id -u):$(id -g)`), **or** make the kubeconfig readable.
2. Make sure your local `~/.kube/config` points at the Cobra cluster (`oc login ...` on this host first), otherwise the build will have nothing to talk to.

```bash
# on E-5CG2310LQ9 — only if this host has oc login to Cobra
docker rm -f rca-agent
docker run -d --name rca-agent --restart unless-stopped --network host \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e RCA_CLUSTER_ENABLED=true -e RCA_KUBECONFIG_MODE=local \
  -e RCA_NAMESPACE=plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 \
  -e KUBECONFIG=/kube/config -e RCA_PORT=8004 -e HOME=/tmp \
  -v ~/.kube/config:/kube/config:ro \
  rca-agent:0.3.1
```

The deliberate design here is that the kubeconfig is mounted read-only and the container runs as a non-root uid that must match the file's owner — that's the "kubeconfig is mode 600 → run as the owning uid" gotcha from the earlier working session. On the jumpserver that owner is uid 1744 (`eagamil`); on the build host it's uid 1000 (`milind`).

Which host do you actually want this running on? If it's the jumpserver, use Option A exactly as above. If you were intentionally testing locally and this host has an `oc login` to Cobra, Option B's `--user $(id -u):$(id -g)` will clear the `Permission denied`.

Now I can give you exact instructions. The way you "test the new tools when you see a pod in trouble" is to **POST an Alertmanager payload naming that pod** to `/webhook/alertmanager`. With `cluster_enabled=true`, the agent then calls the real read-only `KubeQueryTools` to pull that pod's live status, events, logs, and recent config/rollout changes, and returns a ranked root-cause `IncidentReport` with citations.

The resolution logic (from `alert.target`): it picks the resource from labels in order `pod → deployment → statefulset → service → job → instance`. And `KubeQueryTools._resolve_pods` matches that name as an exact pod, a workload prefix (`eric-pc-sm` → `eric-pc-sm-...`), or a substring. So you can point it at a specific broken pod or a whole component.

## How to test against a pod in trouble

First, find a pod that's actually unhealthy on the cluster (run on the jumpserver where `oc` is logged in):

```bash
oc get pods -n plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 \
  --field-selector=status.phase!=Running 2>/dev/null
# or spot restarts/crashloops:
oc get pods -n plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 \
  -o wide | sort -k4 -nr | head
```

Then POST an alert naming that pod (replace `POD_NAME`). Run this from wherever you can reach port 8004 (the jumpserver itself, or your laptop through the SSH tunnel):

```bash
curl -s -X POST localhost:8004/webhook/alertmanager \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "version": "4",
    "status": "firing",
    "receiver": "rca-agent",
    "alerts": [
      {
        "status": "firing",
        "labels": {
          "alertname": "PodUnhealthy",
          "namespace": "plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301",
          "pod": "POD_NAME",
          "severity": "critical"
        },
        "annotations": { "description": "pod in trouble - investigate" },
        "startsAt": "2026-10-26T23:05:00Z"
      }
    ]
  }' | python3 -m json.tool
```

The response is the `IncidentReport`: `symptom`, ranked `hypotheses`, `blast_radius`, an `evidence` list, and `suggested_next_steps`. Key fields to look at:

- **`evidence`** — this is the proof the new `KubeQueryTools` pulled live: the pod's `last_termination_reason` (e.g. `OOMKilled`), restart counts, warning events, log lines (fenced as untrusted), and any `recent_changes` (configmap/secret edits, rollouts) in the correlation window.
- **`hypotheses`** — ranked candidate causes derived from that evidence.

## Important caveat for *your* cluster

Two things will shape what you get back, and you should verify them rather than assume:

1. **`namespace` must be the real namespace** (`plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301`), not `open5gs` from the sample fixture. The pipeline uses `alert.namespace` to scope the queries. The sample fixture uses `open5gs` and pod `upf-0`, which won't exist on Cobra.

2. **`pods/log` RBAC** — reading logs needs the `pods/log` subresource. If the `eagamil` token can't read it, you'll see a `cannot read logs ...` warning and the `evidence` will still include status/events/changes but no log lines. That's graceful degradation, not a failure. You can check with:
   ```bash
   oc auth can-i get pods/log -n plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301
   ```

## Two ways to confirm the new tools are really being exercised

- **No-cluster sanity check first** (proves the webhook + report shape work, using the built-in stub scenario): POST the sample fixture to a cluster-disabled instance — it returns the canned UPF-OOMKilled→SMF story. On your current cluster-enabled container, that same POST instead hits the live cluster.
- **Watch the logs while you POST**: `docker logs -f rca-agent` on the jumpserver. When the alert comes in you'll see `processed 1/1 firing alerts`, and any `skipping ... 403` / `cannot read logs` warnings tell you exactly which live calls succeeded.

One correction to set expectations: the `reasoning_mode=llm` path is still a **pass-through** (Phase 2 TODO) — it does not yet re-rank with an LLM. So the ranking and evidence you get are from the deterministic extractive pipeline regardless of mode. That's by design (rules-first), and it's the part that's fully working now.

Want me to add a tiny helper script (`send-test-alert.sh <pod> [namespace] [port]`) to the package so you can fire a test alert at any pod without hand-editing JSON?

Now I can explain precisely. The code confirms:

- **`hypotheses` and `evidence`** are built *only* from live tool output (`pod_status`, `recent_events`, `logs`, `recent_changes`) and the graph. Nothing there is canned. If the cluster is unreachable, these come back **empty**.
- **`suggested_next_steps`** are built by `build_next_steps`, which queries the `StubRunbookRetriever` using the top hypothesis (or, when there are no hypotheses, the alert name + resource) as the search query. The stub keyword-matches against its 3 canned UPF/SMF/ConfigMap runbooks and returns whatever overlaps.

So here's what happened in your run:

**The runbook suggestions are hardcoded demo data — they did NOT come from Cobra.** They're keyword-matched to your alert text (your alert mentioned SMF/UPF/PFCP, or the stub just returned its defaults). The presence of "fake UPF" runbooks does not mean the agent saw a UPF on Cobra. It only means the runbook RAG is still the stub (Phase 2 not built, and no `RCA_RUNBOOK_RAG_URL` configured).

The question that actually matters — did the agent read real Cobra pod data? — is answered by the **`evidence`** and **`hypotheses`** arrays, not `suggested_next_steps`. Given your earlier `Permission denied: /kube/config` → `nodes: 0` empty graph, I strongly suspect those two arrays came back **empty or near-empty**, meaning the agent never reached the cluster. Please paste the full report (especially `evidence` and `hypotheses`), or just:

```bash

curl -s -X POST localhost:8004/webhook/alertmanager -H 'content-type: application/json' -d @alert.json \
```

FROM python:3.12-slim AS base

ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1

WORKDIR /app

# Install dependencies first for better layer caching.
COPY pyproject.toml README.md ./
COPY src ./src

# Install core + cluster + viz extras:
#   cluster -> kubernetes client (reach the cluster)
#   viz     -> pyvis (interactive /graph/view HTML)
RUN pip install --upgrade pip && pip install ".[cluster,viz]"

# Bind to all interfaces inside the container so the published port works.
ENV RCA_HOST=0.0.0.0 \
    RCA_PORT=8080

# Run as a non-root user (matches the Helm securityContext).
RUN useradd -u 10001 -r -s /usr/sbin/nologin appuser
USER 10001

EXPOSE 8080

CMD ["rca-agent"]

image:
  repository: rca-agent
  tag: "0.1.0"
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent

replicaCount: 1

# The namespace holding the 5G core to monitor.
monitorNamespace: open5gs

agent:
  reasoningMode: extractive   # extractive | llm
  clusterEnabled: true        # use the read-only kube client in-cluster
  logLevel: INFO
  runbookRagUrl: ""           # existing doc-intelligence RAG service URL

service:
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 8080

# Read-only RBAC. The ClusterRole grants ONLY get/list/watch — no write verbs
# exist, so even a compromised/confused LLM cannot mutate the cluster.
rbac:
  create: true

serviceAccount:
  create: true
  name: ""   # defaults to the release name

resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 100m
    memory: 128Mi
  limits:
    cpu: 500m
    memory: 512Mi

# Harden the pod: non-root, read-only root FS, no privilege escalation.
securityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 10001
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  capabilities:
    drop: ["ALL"]

apiVersion: v2
name: rca-agent
description: Read-only Kubernetes fault detection & root-cause agent for a 5G core.
type: application
version: 0.1.0
appVersion: "0.1.0"
keywords:
  - observability
  - root-cause
  - 5g
  - graphrag
  - read-only

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ include "rca-agent.fullname" . }}
  labels:
    {{- include "rca-agent.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "rca-agent.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        {{- include "rca-agent.selectorLabels" . | nindent 8 }}
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: {{ include "rca-agent.serviceAccountName" . }}
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: {{ .Values.securityContext.runAsNonRoot }}
        runAsUser: {{ .Values.securityContext.runAsUser }}
      containers:
        - name: rca-agent
          image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
          imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.image.pullPolicy }}
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: {{ .Values.service.port }}
          env:
            - name: RCA_PORT
              value: "{{ .Values.service.port }}"
            - name: RCA_REASONING_MODE
              value: "{{ .Values.agent.reasoningMode }}"
            - name: RCA_CLUSTER_ENABLED
              value: "{{ .Values.agent.clusterEnabled }}"
            - name: RCA_NAMESPACE
              value: "{{ .Values.monitorNamespace }}"
            - name: RCA_LOG_LEVEL
              value: "{{ .Values.agent.logLevel }}"
            - name: RCA_RUNBOOK_RAG_URL
              value: "{{ .Values.agent.runbookRagUrl }}"
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: {{ .Values.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation }}
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: {{ .Values.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem }}
            capabilities:
              {{- toYaml .Values.securityContext.capabilities | nindent 14 }}
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 15
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          resources:
            {{- toYaml .Values.resources | nindent 12 }}

{{- if .Values.serviceAccount.create }}
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: {{ include "rca-agent.serviceAccountName" . }}
  labels:
    {{- include "rca-agent.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
{{- end }}
---
{{- if .Values.rbac.create }}
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: {{ include "rca-agent.fullname" . }}-readonly
  labels:
    {{- include "rca-agent.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
# READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION: only get/list/watch. No create/update/patch/delete.
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources:
      - pods
      - pods/log
      - services
      - endpoints
      - events
      - configmaps
      - secrets
      - persistentvolumeclaims
      - nodes
      - namespaces
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
  - apiGroups: ["apps"]
    resources:
      - deployments
      - replicasets
      - statefulsets
      - daemonsets
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
  - apiGroups: ["batch"]
    resources: ["jobs", "cronjobs"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
  - apiGroups: ["metrics.k8s.io"]
    resources: ["pods", "nodes"]
    verbs: ["get", "list"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: {{ include "rca-agent.fullname" . }}-readonly
  labels:
    {{- include "rca-agent.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: {{ include "rca-agent.fullname" . }}-readonly
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: {{ include "rca-agent.serviceAccountName" . }}
    namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
{{- end }}

Kubernetes Fault Detection & Root-Cause Agent (POC). Read-only agent that builds
a live dependency graph of a 5G core on Kubernetes/OpenShift and (later) explains
root causes. This session: **scaffolded the project, implemented live cluster
graph generation, containerized it, and ran it successfully against a real
OpenShift cluster (Cobra 2a), rendering an interactive graph.**

Project root: `/home/milind/telco-k8s-rca-agent`
venv: `.venv` (Python 3.12). Build host: `E-5CG2310LQ9` (has docker/podman).

---

## MILESTONE REACHED ✅

The agent ran as a Docker container on the Cobra jumpserver and built a live
graph from the real namespace:
```
graph rebuilt from cluster ns=plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 selector=None:
  {'nodes': 1485, 'edges': 2028, 'changes': 3858, ...}
```
Served interactive viz on port 8004, viewed via SSH tunnel from the laptop.

---

## WHAT WAS BUILT

### 1. Full project scaffold (`src/rca_agent/`)
- `config.py` — pydantic-settings, env prefix `RCA_`. Key settings:
  `cluster_enabled`, `kubeconfig_mode` (auto/incluster/local), `namespace`,
  `nf_selector` (empty = whole namespace), `reasoning_mode` (extractive default),
  `graph_rebuild_interval_seconds` (60), `runbook_rag_url`, host/port.
- `models/` — `Alert`/`AlertmanagerPayload`/`KubeEvent` (inputs);
  `IncidentReport`/`Hypothesis`/`Evidence`/`Citation`/`Severity` (output).

  change log. `NodeKind`, `EdgeKind` (calls/runs_on/mounts/managed_by/selects),
  `Health` enum (healthy/degraded/down/unknown). `roll_up_health()`,
  `managed_pods()`, `upstream()/downstream()`, `neighborhood()`, `build_demo_graph()`.
- `graph/builder.py` — `GraphBuilder._rebuild_from_cluster()`: discovers
  nodes/workloads/replicasets/pods/configmaps/secrets/pvcs/services; builds
  runs_on/managed_by/mounts/selects edges; pod health from phase+container
  statuses (OOMKilled/CrashLoopBackOff/readiness); rolls up to workload.
  **Permission-tolerant** via `_safe_list()` (403/forbidden on a resource type is
  skipped with a warning, not fatal).
- `tools/kube_client.py` — read-only client bootstrap, auto/incluster/local
  config detection. kubernetes pkg imported lazily (in `[cluster]` extra).
- `tools/query_tools.py` — `StubQueryTools` (demo evidence). `get_query_tools`
  FALLS BACK to stub even when cluster_enabled (KubeQueryTools NOT yet built).
- `reasoning/` — extractive pipeline (triage→gather→graph_walk→change_correlation
  →hypothesize_rank→report) + LangGraph flow wrapper (falls back to extractive).
- `rag/runbook_retriever.py` — `StubRunbookRetriever` (keyword) + HTTP stub.
- `webhook/app.py` — FastAPI. Endpoints: `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/graph/stats`,
  `/graph/neighborhood/{node}`, `/graph/view` (+ `?hide_orphans`),
  `/graph/view/{node}?radius=`, `/webhook/alertmanager`, `/docs`.

  shaped by kind; edges labeled by relationship. **Physics freezes after layout**
  (stops drifting); **orphan (edgeless) nodes hidden by default** on full view.

### 2. Demo graph is pod-centric (fixed mid-session)

(one OOMKilled → workload degraded), pods runs_on nodes / mount cm+secret+pvc,
service selects pods. Matches real cluster builder output. No NF `calls` edges

`s7427-Cobra-JS` = `10.242.70.7`, user `eagamil` (uid/gid 1744, in docker group),
RHEL 8.8, has docker. OpenShift cluster: Cobra 2a
`https://api.cobra-2a-openshift.bete.ericy.com:6443`.
Target namespace: `plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301` (cSAEGW-C). Port: **8004**.

**NOTE:** mop-tool's login scripts (`/home/milind/mop-tool/scripts/cobra-login.sh`)
contain the OCP creds (`oc login ... -u eagamil -p <REDACTED-PASSWORD>
--insecure-skip-tls-verify`). Those scripts hold HARDCODED PRODUCTION SECRETS —
handle carefully. We reuse the MECHANISM (oc login → token kubeconfig), not copy
secrets into this project.

### Run sequence (reproduced & working)
```bash
# 1. laptop -> copy image to jumpserver
scp /home/milind/rca-agent-0.1.0.tar.gz eagamil@10.242.70.7:~/

# 2. jumpserver: oc login (writes token kubeconfig to ~/.kube/config)
oc login https://api.cobra-2a-openshift.bete.ericy.com:6443 -u eagamil -p <REDACTED-PASSWORD> --insecure-skip-tls-verify

# 3. jumpserver: load + run (SINGLE LINE to avoid paste corruption)
docker rm -f rca-agent
docker load -i ~/rca-agent-0.1.0.tar.gz
docker run -d --name rca-agent --network host --user 1744:1744 -e RCA_CLUSTER_ENABLED=true -e RCA_KUBECONFIG_MODE=local -e RCA_NAMESPACE=plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 -e KUBECONFIG=/kube/config -e RCA_PORT=8004 -e HOME=/tmp -v ~/.kube/config:/kube/config:ro rca-agent:0.1.0
docker logs -f rca-agent

# 4. laptop: tunnel + view
ssh -L 8004:localhost:8004 eagamil@10.242.70.7
#   http://localhost:8004/graph/view        (full, frozen, orphans hidden)
#   http://localhost:8004/graph/view/<pod>?radius=2
#   http://localhost:8004/graph/stats
```

### Key gotchas solved this session
- `--network host` needed so the API server URL resolves from inside container.
- kubeconfig is mode 600 (eagamil-only) → run container as `--user 1744:1744`
  + `-e HOME=/tmp` so uid 1744 can read the mounted config. (NOT chmod 644.)
- Multi-line `docker run` got corrupted on paste → use SINGLE-LINE command.
- `InsecureRequestWarning` in logs = harmless (TLS verify off from oc login).
- Startup no longer crashes on kube errors (serves empty graph, retries).

---

## REAL CLUSTER FINDINGS (cSAEGW-C / Ericsson PCC)

Namespace = ONE Helm umbrella release (`eric-cloud-native-base` chart 368.1.2,
"PCC 1.42 CP0 rev PA28"). 1485 nodes total. Label hierarchy on pods:
- `app.kubernetes.io/instance` / `release` = whole release (≈ namespace)
- **`app.kubernetes.io/name` = individual component** ← use THIS to group/list
- `statefulset.kubernetes.io/pod-name` = individual pod
- `applicationId` (= `plantx2avzwcpcsm-y-oc-conss-002`, note: value mismatches
  the namespace — templating artifact) = WHOLE-deployment identity, in
  metrics/licensing config, NOT a reliable per-pod label. Use only as graph-level
  metadata, not for component grouping.

Components present (from Helm values, enabled):
- **eric-pc-sm** (the SMF/PGW/SGW NF logic): controller, diameter, http-client,
  ip-allocator, notification-forwarder, nsmf-forwarder, sgw-session,
  smf-pgw-session, udp-forwarder, geo-red-forwarder, target-database-master-rd,
  target-database-replica-rd, br-agent.
- Routing/data-plane: eric-pc-routing-engine(-api), eric-pc-routing-aggregator,
  eric-pc-vpn-gateway-forwarder, eric-pc-up-timer-wheel, eric-pc-kvdb-rd-server/operator.
- Platform (eric-cloud-native-base): eric-cm-mediator, eric-ctrl-bro,
  eric-data-* (zk, message-bus-kf, search-engine, object-storage-mn),
  eric-pm-server, eric-sec-* (certm, sip-tls, key-management, ldap),
  eric-fh-* (snmp/alarm), eric-log-transformer, eric-lm-combined-server, etc.
- Disabled (should NOT appear): eric-pc-mm, eric-pc-mm-controller-supervisor,
  eric-sec-access-mgmt.

---

## OPEN ITEMS / NEXT STEPS (circle back tomorrow)

1. **Component listing view** (user asked, agreed approach C): group 1485 nodes by
   `app.kubernetes.io/name`. Build:
   - builder: capture `app.kubernetes.io/name` label onto each pod as a
     `component` attr; also capture `applicationId` as graph-level metadata.
   - `GET /graph/components` → [{component, pods, healthy, health}] summary list.
   - `GET /graph/view/component/<name>` → that component's pod subgraph.
   This is the proper way to navigate so many nodes.
2. **Scope via selector** meanwhile: `-e RCA_NF_SELECTOR=app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter`
   (empty = whole namespace). List components:
   `oc get pods -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.labels.app\.kubernetes\.io/name}{"\n"}{end}' | sort -u`
3. **Silence InsecureRequestWarning** (urllib3.disable_warnings) for clean logs.
4. **KubeQueryTools** not implemented — reasoning uses stub evidence when cluster
   enabled. Needed for real root-cause (pod status/logs/metrics/changes from cluster).
5. Future: in-cluster pod deployment (Helm chart ready, read-only SA); event watcher;
   Alertmanager rules; chaos eval; Streamlit UI; token-expiry handling (oc login
   token ~24h → re-login, or use a ServiceAccount token).

## DESIGN INVARIANTS
Read-only (get/list/watch only, no write tool). Rules-first (deterministic evidence;
LLM only ranks/explains). Pod-centric graph with health rollup. Permission-tolerant.
Everything cited. Untrusted log text fenced.

"""Application settings.

All configuration is read from environment variables (prefix ``RCA_``) or a
local ``.env`` file. Defaults are chosen so the agent runs out-of-the-box in
no-LLM extractive mode without a cluster connection.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import Field
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_prefix="RCA_",
        env_file=".env",
        env_file_encoding="utf-8",
        extra="ignore",
    )

    # --- Service ---
    app_name: str = "k8s-rca-agent"
    host: str = "0.0.0.0"
    port: int = 8080
    log_level: str = "INFO"

    # --- Reasoning mode ---
    # "extractive" = deterministic, no LLM (default; reproducible & cheap).
    # "llm"        = LLM ranks/explains the rule-gathered evidence.
    reasoning_mode: Literal["extractive", "llm"] = "extractive"

    # --- Cluster access ---
    # When False, graph/query tools use stubbed/in-memory data (safe for demos
    # and CI). When True, the kubernetes client is used in read-only fashion.
    cluster_enabled: bool = False

    # How to load kube config:
    #   "auto"      — in-cluster if a ServiceAccount token is present, else kubeconfig
    #   "incluster" — force the mounted ServiceAccount token (normal in-pod path)
    #   "local"     — force the local kubeconfig (dev from a jumphost/laptop)
    kubeconfig_mode: Literal["auto", "incluster", "local"] = "auto"

    namespace: str = Field(
        default="open5gs",
        description="Namespace holding the NF/application to monitor.",
    )

    # Label selector scoping the monitored application within the namespace.
    # Empty (default) = the whole namespace is treated as the one application.
    # Narrow it later to a single NF, e.g. "app=upf" or "app.kubernetes.io/name=upf".
    nf_selector: str = ""

    # --- Graph ---
    graph_rebuild_interval_seconds: int = 60
    graph_history_window_minutes: int = 120

    # --- Evidence gathering ---
    log_tail_lines: int = 200
    change_correlation_window_minutes: int = 15

    # Optional Prometheus base URL for the metrics() query tool. When unset,
    # metrics are skipped gracefully (pod status/events/logs/changes still work).
    prometheus_url: str | None = None

    # --- RAG runbook retriever ---
    runbook_rag_url: str | None = None  # existing doc-intelligence service
    runbook_rag_top_k: int = 3

    # --- LLM (only used when reasoning_mode == "llm") ---
    llm_provider: str = "none"
    llm_model: str | None = None


@lru_cache
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    """Return a cached Settings instance."""
    return Settings()

"""Read-only Kubernetes fault detection & root-cause agent for a 5G core.

The agent detects faults (via Alertmanager webhook and Kubernetes events),
gathers evidence, reasons over a live NetworkX dependency graph, and emits an
incident report with ranked root-cause hypotheses. It never mutates the cluster.
"""

__version__ = "0.3.0"

   - builder: capture `app.kubernetes.io/name` label onto each pod as a
     `component` attr; also capture `applicationId` as graph-level metadata.
   - `GET /graph/components` → [{component, pods, healthy, health}] summary list.
   - `GET /graph/view/component/<name>` → that component's pod subgraph.
   This is the proper way to navigate so many nodes.
2. **Scope via selector** meanwhile: `-e RCA_NF_SELECTOR=app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter`
   (empty = whole namespace). List components:
   `oc get pods -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.labels.app\.kubernetes\.io/name}{"\n"}{end}' | sort -u`
3. **Silence InsecureRequestWarning** (urllib3.disable_warnings) for clean logs.
4. **KubeQueryTools** not implemented — reasoning uses stub evidence when cluster
   enabled. Needed for real root-cause (pod status/logs/metrics/changes from cluster).
5. Future: in-cluster pod deployment (Helm chart ready, read-only SA); event watcher;
   Alertmanager rules; chaos eval; Streamlit UI; token-expiry handling (oc login
   token ~24h → re-login, or use a ServiceAccount token).

## DESIGN INVARIANTS
Read-only (get/list/watch only, no write tool). Rules-first (deterministic evidence;
LLM only ranks/explains). Pod-centric graph with health rollup. Permission-tolerant.
Everything cited. Untrusted log text fenced.

"""Application settings.

All configuration is read from environment variables (prefix ``RCA_``) or a
local ``.env`` file. Defaults are chosen so the agent runs out-of-the-box in
no-LLM extractive mode without a cluster connection.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import Field
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_prefix="RCA_",
        env_file=".env",
        env_file_encoding="utf-8",
        extra="ignore",
    )

    # --- Service ---
    app_name: str = "k8s-rca-agent"
    host: str = "0.0.0.0"
    port: int = 8080
    log_level: str = "INFO"

    # --- Reasoning mode ---
    # "extractive" = deterministic, no LLM (default; reproducible & cheap).
    # "llm"        = LLM ranks/explains the rule-gathered evidence.
    reasoning_mode: Literal["extractive", "llm"] = "extractive"

    # --- Cluster access ---
    # When False, graph/query tools use stubbed/in-memory data (safe for demos
    # and CI). When True, the kubernetes client is used in read-only fashion.
    cluster_enabled: bool = False

    # How to load kube config:
    #   "auto"      — in-cluster if a ServiceAccount token is present, else kubeconfig
    #   "incluster" — force the mounted ServiceAccount token (normal in-pod path)
    #   "local"     — force the local kubeconfig (dev from a jumphost/laptop)
    kubeconfig_mode: Literal["auto", "incluster", "local"] = "auto"

    namespace: str = Field(
        default="open5gs",
        description="Namespace holding the NF/application to monitor.",
    )

    # Label selector scoping the monitored application within the namespace.
    # Empty (default) = the whole namespace is treated as the one application.
    # Narrow it later to a single NF, e.g. "app=upf" or "app.kubernetes.io/name=upf".
    nf_selector: str = ""

    # --- Graph ---
    graph_rebuild_interval_seconds: int = 60
    graph_history_window_minutes: int = 120

    # --- Evidence gathering ---
    log_tail_lines: int = 200
    change_correlation_window_minutes: int = 15

    # Optional Prometheus base URL for the metrics() query tool. When unset,
    # metrics are skipped gracefully (pod status/events/logs/changes still work).
    prometheus_url: str | None = None

    # --- RAG runbook retriever ---
    runbook_rag_url: str | None = None  # existing doc-intelligence service
    runbook_rag_top_k: int = 3

    # --- LLM (only used when reasoning_mode == "llm") ---
    llm_provider: str = "none"
    llm_model: str | None = None


@lru_cache
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    """Return a cached Settings instance."""
    return Settings()

"""Read-only Kubernetes fault detection & root-cause agent for a 5G core.

The agent detects faults (via Alertmanager webhook and Kubernetes events),
gathers evidence, reasons over a live NetworkX dependency graph, and emits an
incident report with ranked root-cause hypotheses. It never mutates the cluster.
"""

__version__ = "0.3.0"

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "k8s-rca-agent"
version = "0.3.0"
description = "Read-only Kubernetes fault detection & root-cause agent for a 5G core (GraphRAG-style reasoning over a live dependency graph)."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }
authors = [{ name = "Milind" }]

dependencies = [
    "fastapi>=0.110",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.29",
    "pydantic>=2.6",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.2",
    "networkx>=3.2",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "python-dateutil>=2.9",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# LangGraph reasoning + LLM ranking. The core runs fine in no-LLM extractive mode without these.
llm = [
    "langgraph>=0.2",
    "langchain-core>=0.3",
]
# Live cluster access (Alertmanager/event watchers, kube queries).
cluster = [
    "kubernetes>=29.0",
]
# Interactive graph visualization (pyvis -> vis.js HTML).
viz = [
    "pyvis>=0.3.2",
]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "ruff>=0.4",
    "pyvis>=0.3.2",
]

[project.scripts]
rca-agent = "rca_agent.webhook.app:main"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py310"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["src"]
testpaths = ["tests"]

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# deploy-cobra.sh — load & run the read-only rca-agent 0.3.0 on the Cobra jumpserver.
#
# This script is intended to run ON the Cobra jumpserver (s7427-Cobra-JS, 10.242.70.7)
# as user eagamil (uid/gid 1744, member of the docker group), after you have run
# `oc login` so that ~/.kube/config holds a valid token kubeconfig.
#
# It is READ-ONLY by construction: the agent only ever does get/list/watch against
# the cluster. It never mutates anything.
#
# Usage:
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh                 # verify checksum, load image, (re)start container, tail logs
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh --no-logs       # same but do not tail logs at the end
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh --skip-verify   # skip sha256 verification (not recommended)
#
# Override any default via environment variable, e.g.:
#   RCA_NAMESPACE=some-other-ns RCA_PORT=8005 ./deploy-cobra.sh
#   RCA_NF_SELECTOR='app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter' ./deploy-cobra.sh
#
set -euo pipefail

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration (override via environment)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
IMAGE_NAME="${IMAGE_NAME:-rca-agent}"
IMAGE_TAG="${IMAGE_TAG:-0.3.0}"
IMAGE_REF="${IMAGE_NAME}:${IMAGE_TAG}"

CONTAINER_NAME="${CONTAINER_NAME:-rca-agent}"

# Default target matches Cobra 2a / cSAEGW-C.
RCA_NAMESPACE="${RCA_NAMESPACE:-plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301}"
RCA_PORT="${RCA_PORT:-8004}"
# Empty selector = whole namespace. Narrow to one component to shrink the graph,
# e.g. RCA_NF_SELECTOR='app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter'
RCA_NF_SELECTOR="${RCA_NF_SELECTOR:-}"
RCA_REASONING_MODE="${RCA_REASONING_MODE:-extractive}"

# The uid:gid the container runs as. Must match the owner of ~/.kube/config
# (mode 600) so the mounted kubeconfig is readable. On Cobra that is 1744:1744.
RUN_UID_GID="${RUN_UID_GID:-1744:1744}"

# Path to the kubeconfig written by `oc login` on the jumpserver.
KUBECONFIG_HOST="${KUBECONFIG_HOST:-$HOME/.kube/config}"

# Artifacts shipped alongside this script.
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
IMAGE_TARBALL="${IMAGE_TARBALL:-$SCRIPT_DIR/rca-agent-${IMAGE_TAG}.tar.gz}"
SHA_FILE="${SHA_FILE:-${IMAGE_TARBALL}.sha256}"

SKIP_VERIFY=0
TAIL_LOGS=1
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --skip-verify) SKIP_VERIFY=1 ;;
    --no-logs)     TAIL_LOGS=0 ;;
    -h|--help)
      grep '^#' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "WARN: unknown arg '$arg' (ignored)" >&2 ;;
  esac
done

log()  { printf '\033[1;34m[deploy]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[error]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { err "$*"; exit 1; }

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pre-flight checks
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "docker not found on PATH."
docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "cannot talk to the docker daemon (is '$USER' in the docker group?)."

[ -f "$IMAGE_TARBALL" ] || die "image tarball not found: $IMAGE_TARBALL"

if [ ! -f "$KUBECONFIG_HOST" ]; then
  die "kubeconfig not found at $KUBECONFIG_HOST. Run 'oc login <api-url> -u <user> -p <pass> --insecure-skip-tls-verify' first."
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Verify checksum
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$SKIP_VERIFY" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ -f "$SHA_FILE" ]; then
    log "verifying sha256 of $(basename "$IMAGE_TARBALL") ..."
    ( cd "$(dirname "$IMAGE_TARBALL")" && sha256sum -c "$(basename "$SHA_FILE")" ) \
      || die "checksum verification FAILED — tarball is corrupt or truncated. Re-copy it."
    log "checksum OK."
  else
    err "no .sha256 sidecar found ($SHA_FILE); skipping verification."
  fi
else
  log "checksum verification skipped (--skip-verify)."
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load the image
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "loading image $IMAGE_REF from $(basename "$IMAGE_TARBALL") ..."
docker load -i "$IMAGE_TARBALL"
docker image inspect "$IMAGE_REF" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || die "image $IMAGE_REF not present after load (tarball tag mismatch?)."

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. (Re)start the container
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "removing any existing container named '$CONTAINER_NAME' ..."
docker rm -f "$CONTAINER_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

log "starting $CONTAINER_NAME (ns=$RCA_NAMESPACE port=$RCA_PORT user=$RUN_UID_GID selector='${RCA_NF_SELECTOR:-<whole-namespace>}') ..."
# NOTES on the flags (learned from earlier sessions):
#   --network host  : so the OpenShift API server URL resolves/reaches from inside.
#   --user 1744:1744: so the mounted (mode 600) kubeconfig is readable by the process.
#   -e HOME=/tmp    : uid 1744 has no /etc/passwd home inside the image; give it a writable one.
#   -v ...:ro       : kubeconfig mounted read-only.
docker run -d \
  --name "$CONTAINER_NAME" \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --network host \
  --user "$RUN_UID_GID" \
  -e RCA_CLUSTER_ENABLED=true \
  -e RCA_KUBECONFIG_MODE=local \
  -e RCA_NAMESPACE="$RCA_NAMESPACE" \
  -e RCA_NF_SELECTOR="$RCA_NF_SELECTOR" \
  -e RCA_REASONING_MODE="$RCA_REASONING_MODE" \
  -e RCA_PORT="$RCA_PORT" \
  -e KUBECONFIG=/kube/config \
  -e HOME=/tmp \
  -v "$KUBECONFIG_HOST":/kube/config:ro \
  "$IMAGE_REF"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Health check
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "waiting for the agent to answer /healthz on port $RCA_PORT ..."
ok=0
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do
  if curl -fsS "http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/healthz" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok=1; break
  fi
  sleep 1
done

if [ "$ok" -eq 1 ]; then
  log "healthy: $(curl -fsS "http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/healthz")"
  log "stats:   $(curl -fsS "http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/stats" || echo '(not ready yet — first cluster build may take ~a minute)')"
  cat <<EOF

  ✅ rca-agent ${IMAGE_TAG} is running.

  View from your LAPTOP via an SSH tunnel:
      ssh -L ${RCA_PORT}:localhost:${RCA_PORT} eagamil@10.242.70.7
  then open:
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/view                 (full graph; orphans hidden)
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/components            (components grouped by app.kubernetes.io/name)
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/view/component/<name> (one component's subgraph)
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/view/<pod>?radius=2   (neighborhood of a pod)
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/stats
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/docs                        (OpenAPI)

  Manage:
      docker logs -f ${CONTAINER_NAME}
      docker rm -f ${CONTAINER_NAME}
EOF
else
  err "agent did not become healthy on port ${RCA_PORT}. Recent logs:"
  docker logs --tail 40 "$CONTAINER_NAME" || true
  die "startup health check failed."
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Tail logs (optional)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$TAIL_LOGS" -eq 1 ]; then
  log "tailing logs (Ctrl-C to detach; container keeps running) ..."
  docker logs -f "$CONTAINER_NAME"
fi

"""FastAPI application. Endpoints: GET /healthz liveness GET /readyz readiness (graph built) GET /graph/stats current dependency-graph stats POST /webhook/alertmanager Alertmanager v4 webhook -> incident report(s) The app builds the dependency graph once at startup (demo graph with no cluster) and reuses it across requests. Each firing alert is reasoned about independently and returned as an IncidentReport. """ from __future__ import annotations import asyncio import contextlib import logging from contextlib import asynccontextmanager from fastapi import FastAPI from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse from pydantic import BaseModel from rca_agent import __version__ from rca_agent.config import get_settings from rca_agent.graph.builder import GraphBuilder from rca_agent.models.alert import AlertmanagerPayload from rca_agent.models.incident import IncidentReport from rca_agent.reasoning.flow import ReasoningFlow logger = logging.getLogger("rca_agent") settings = get_settings() # Shared state. """Read-only Kubernetes client bootstrap.

Config is loaded one of three ways, selected by ``kubeconfig_mode``:

* ``incluster`` — use the mounted ServiceAccount token (the normal in-pod
  deployment path). Safety rests on the restricted ClusterRole bound to that SA.
* ``local`` — use the local kubeconfig (dev iteration from a jumphost/laptop).
* ``auto`` (default) — in-cluster if the ServiceAccount token is present, else
  fall back to kubeconfig. The same build therefore works both ways with no
  code change.

The client is used read-only: only ``list_*`` / ``read_*`` calls are ever made.
The ``kubernetes`` dependency lives in the ``[cluster]`` extra, so it is imported
lazily — the no-cluster/demo path never needs it installed.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass

logger = logging.getLogger("rca_agent.kube")

# Standard in-pod ServiceAccount token mount path.
_SA_TOKEN_PATH = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"


@dataclass
class KubeClient:
    """Thin holder for the read-only typed API clients."""

    core: object  # kubernetes.client.CoreV1Api
    apps: object  # kubernetes.client.AppsV1Api
    mode: str     # how config was loaded: "incluster" | "local"


def _running_in_cluster() -> bool:
    return os.path.exists(_SA_TOKEN_PATH) or bool(os.environ.get("KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST"))


def build_kube_client(mode: str = "auto") -> KubeClient:
    """Load kube config (read-only) and return typed CoreV1Api + AppsV1Api.

    Raises RuntimeError with a clear message if the ``[cluster]`` extra is not
    installed, or if config cannot be loaded for the requested mode.
    """
    try:
        from kubernetes import client, config  # type: ignore
        from kubernetes.config.config_exception import ConfigException  # type: ignore
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - import guard
        raise RuntimeError(
            "The kubernetes client is not installed. Install the cluster extra: "
            "pip install '.[cluster]'"
        ) from exc

    loaded_mode = _load_config(config, ConfigException, mode)
    logger.info("kube config loaded via %s", loaded_mode)
    return KubeClient(core=client.CoreV1Api(), apps=client.AppsV1Api(), mode=loaded_mode)


def _load_config(config, ConfigException, mode: str) -> str:
    """Load kube config for the requested mode; return the effective mode."""
    if mode not in ("auto", "incluster", "local"):
        raise RuntimeError(f"invalid kubeconfig_mode: {mode!r}")

items.Text:
"""Read-only Kubernetes client bootstrap.

Config is loaded one of three ways, selected by ``kubeconfig_mode``:

* ``incluster`` — use the mounted ServiceAccount token (the normal in-pod
  deployment path). Safety rests on the restricted ClusterRole bound to that SA.
* ``local`` — use the local kubeconfig (dev iteration from a jumphost/laptop).
* ``auto`` (default) — in-cluster if the ServiceAccount token is present, else
  fall back to kubeconfig. The same build therefore works both ways with no
  code change.

The client is used read-only: only ``list_*`` / ``read_*`` calls are ever made.
The ``kubernetes`` dependency lives in the ``[cluster]`` extra, so it is imported
lazily — the no-cluster/demo path never needs it installed.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass

logger = logging.getLogger("rca_agent.kube")

# Standard in-pod ServiceAccount token mount path.
_SA_TOKEN_PATH = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"


@dataclass
class KubeClient:
    """Thin holder for the read-only typed API clients."""

    core: object  # kubernetes.client.CoreV1Api
    apps: object  # kubernetes.client.AppsV1Api
    mode: str     # how config was loaded: "incluster" | "local"


def _running_in_cluster() -> bool:
    return os.path.exists(_SA_TOKEN_PATH) or bool(os.environ.get("KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST"))


def build_kube_client(mode: str = "auto") -> KubeClient:
    """Load kube config (read-only) and return typed CoreV1Api + AppsV1Api.

    Raises RuntimeError with a clear message if the ``[cluster]`` extra is not
    installed, or if config cannot be loaded for the requested mode.
    """
    try:
        from kubernetes import client, config  # type: ignore
        from kubernetes.config.config_exception import ConfigException  # type: ignore
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - import guard
        raise RuntimeError(
            "The kubernetes client is not installed. Install the cluster extra: "
            "pip install '.[cluster]'"
        ) from exc

    loaded_mode = _load_config(config, ConfigException, mode)
    logger.info("kube config loaded via %s", loaded_mode)
    return KubeClient(core=client.CoreV1Api(), apps=client.AppsV1Api(), mode=loaded_mode)


def _load_config(config, ConfigException, mode: str) -> str:
    """Load kube config for the requested mode; return the effective mode."""
    if mode not in ("auto", "incluster", "local"):
        raise RuntimeError(f"invalid kubeconfig_mode: {mode!r}")

    if mode in ("auto", "incluster") and _running_in_cluster():
        try:
            config.load_incluster_config()
            return "incluster"
        except ConfigException:
            if mode == "incluster":
                raise
            # auto: fall through to local

    if mode == "incluster":
        raise RuntimeError(
            "kubeconfig_mode=incluster but no in-cluster ServiceAccount token found."
        )

    try:
        config.load_kube_config()
        return "local"
    except ConfigException as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Could not load kubeconfig (local mode). Set KUBECONFIG or run in-cluster."
        ) from exc

This reframes the problem. The real issue is: **the initial synchronous build at import time is slow/blocking against this large namespace, so uvicorn hasn't started serving yet** (or a list call is hanging with no timeout). That's a latent problem equally present in 0.2.0 — your memory of "0.2.0 worked" may have been with a narrower selector, or you waited longer, or it eventually completed.

Two things I need confirmed from the jumpserver to finalize the diagnosis (please paste):

If the container is **Up** but `/healthz` times out, the synchronous startup build is still grinding through the big namespace. If it **Exited**, it was killed (likely OOM on the large list).

Regardless of which, the fix is the same and is a genuine improvement I can make now: **make the initial graph build non-blocking and the cluster list calls bounded** (request timeout + server-side pagination + optionally default to a selector). That makes `/healthz` and `/graph/view` come up immediately and the graph populate in the background — which is what the design (`_safe_rebuild` + background `_refresh_loop`) already intends, except the *first* build runs synchronously at import.

Root cause confirmed by reading the code: `_safe_rebuild()` runs **synchronously at module import** (line 50), and the lifespan handler calls `_safe_rebuild()` **again** synchronously **before** `yield` (line ~78). So uvicorn cannot accept connections until the full 1485-object cluster build finishes. With unpaginated list calls and no client timeout against this large namespace, that first build is slow — so `/healthz` is unavailable and the log stops mid-build. This affects 0.2.0 identically (same build code); 0.3.0 didn't regress it.

The fix (a real improvement, read-only, no design change): make the first build **not block startup** and bound the kube calls. Specifically:
1. In `_lifespan`, run the initial `_safe_rebuild()` in a background thread instead of blocking before `yield`, so `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/graph/view` come up instantly and the graph fills in shortly after.
2. Add a request timeout + server-side pagination to the kube list calls so a huge namespace can't hang or balloon memory.

@asynccontextmanager
async def _lifespan(_: FastAPI):
    logging.basicConfig(level=settings.log_level)
    global _flow
    # Kick off the first graph build WITHOUT blocking startup. A large-namespace
    # cluster build can take a while; running it synchronously here would stop
    # uvicorn from serving /healthz until it finished (and could look like a
    # hang). We build in a background thread and let the refresh loop keep it
    # fresh. With no cluster, this is the instant demo graph.
    async def _initial_build() -> None:
        await asyncio.to_thread(_safe_rebuild)
        global _flow
        _flow = ReasoningFlow(settings, graph=_graph_builder.graph,
                              builder=_graph_builder)
        logger.info("rca-agent initial graph built: %s",
                    _graph_builder.graph.stats())

    logger.info("rca-agent starting: mode=%s cluster=%s (initial graph build "
                "running in background)",
                settings.reasoning_mode, settings.cluster_enabled)
    build_task = asyncio.create_task(_initial_build())
    task = asyncio.create_task(_refresh_loop())
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        for t in (build_task, task):
            t.cancel()
            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await t

# Server-side pagination + per-request timeout keep a huge namespace from
# hanging or ballooning memory on a single unbounded list. The kubernetes
# client accepts ``limit``/``_continue`` for chunked lists and
# ``_request_timeout`` (connect, read) seconds per call.
_LIST_PAGE_SIZE = 500
_LIST_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = (5, 30)  # (connect, read) seconds


def _safe_list(call, label: str):
    """Call a kube ``list_*`` function, tolerating permission/API errors.

    On an OCP namespace a non-admin user is often forbidden from listing some
    resource types (e.g. cluster-scoped ``nodes`` or namespace ``secrets``).
    A single 403 must not blank out the whole graph — we log a warning and
    return an empty list so the rest of the build proceeds.

    The call is paginated server-side (``limit``/``_continue``) and bounded by a
    per-request timeout, so a large namespace completes promptly instead of
    hanging on one unbounded list. ``call`` must accept ``**kw`` so these
    options can be forwarded to the underlying kube ``list_*`` method; if it
    does not (e.g. a test stub), we fall back to a single plain call.
    """
    items: list = []
    cont: str | None = None
    try:
        while True:
            kw = {"limit": _LIST_PAGE_SIZE,
                  "_request_timeout": _LIST_REQUEST_TIMEOUT}
            if cont:
                kw["_continue"] = cont
            try:
                result = call(**kw)
            except TypeError:
                # The call doesn't accept pagination kwargs (test stub / simple
                # lambda) — fall back to one plain call.
                return _items(call())
            items.extend(_items(result))
            meta = getattr(result, "metadata", None)
            cont = getattr(meta, "_continue", None) or getattr(meta, "continue", None)
            if not cont:
                break
        return items
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — tolerate ApiException/403/conn errors
        status = getattr(exc, "status", None)
        reason = getattr(exc, "reason", None) or type(exc).__name__
        logger.warning("skipping %s: cannot list (%s %s)", label, status, reason)
        return []

import time, threading
import rca_agent.webhook.app as appmod

# Simulate a SLOW cluster build to prove startup no longer blocks on it.
slow_started = threading.Event()
slow_done = threading.Event()
def slow_rebuild():

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from rca_agent.webhook.app import app

client = TestClient(app)
FIXTURE = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "alertmanager_sample.json"


def test_healthz():
    r = client.get("/healthz")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json()["status"] == "ok"


def test_graph_stats():
    r = client.get("/graph/stats")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json()["nodes"] > 0


def test_alertmanager_webhook_produces_report():
    payload = json.loads(FIXTURE.read_text())
    r = client.post("/webhook/alertmanager", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["received"] == 1
    assert body["processed"] == 1
    report = body["reports"][0]
    assert report["symptom"]
    assert report["hypotheses"], "expected ranked hypotheses"
    assert report["suggested_next_steps"]


def test_graph_view_returns_html():
    r = client.get("/graph/view")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert "text/html" in r.headers["content-type"]
    assert "vis-network" in r.text or "DataSet" in r.text


def test_graph_view_node_neighborhood():
    r = client.get("/graph/view/upf?radius=2")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert "text/html" in r.headers["content-type"]


def test_graph_view_missing_node_404():
    r = client.get("/graph/view/nope-not-here")
    assert r.status_code == 404

    r = client.get("/graph/view/nope-not-here")

def test_startup_does_not_block_on_graph_build(monkeypatch):
    """The initial graph build must run in the background, not block startup.

    A large-namespace cluster build can be slow; if it ran synchronously in the
    lifespan before ``yield``, uvicorn would not accept connections (and
    ``/healthz`` would hang / connection-refused) until it finished. We simulate
    a slow rebuild and assert ``/healthz`` responds immediately while the build
    is still running in the background.
    """
    import threading
    import time

    import rca_agent.webhook.app as appmod

    started = threading.Event()
    done = threading.Event()
    original = appmod._graph_builder.rebuild

    def slow_rebuild():
        started.set()
        time.sleep(1.5)
        done.set()
        return original()

    monkeypatch.setattr(appmod._graph_builder, "rebuild", slow_rebuild)

    t0 = time.time()
    with TestClient(appmod.app) as local_client:  # triggers lifespan startup
        latency = time.time() - t0
        r = local_client.get("/healthz")
        assert r.status_code == 200
        assert latency < 1.0, f"startup blocked on the graph build ({latency:.2f}s)"
        assert started.is_set(), "background build should have started"
        assert not done.is_set(), "build should still be running (non-blocking)"

"""Cluster-free tests for GraphBuilder._rebuild_from_cluster via a fake client."""
from __future__ import annotations

from rca_agent.config import Settings
from rca_agent.graph.builder import GraphBuilder
from rca_agent.graph.dependency_graph import EdgeKind, Health, NodeKind
from tests import fake_kube as fk


def _settings(selector="") -> Settings:
    return Settings(cluster_enabled=True, namespace="open5gs", nf_selector=selector)


def _store_upf(pod_specs):
    """A UPF app: Deployment -> ReplicaSet -> N pods, a configmap, a node, a service."""
    return {
        "nodes": [fk.node("worker-1"), fk.node("worker-2")],
        "deployments": [fk.deployment("upf", replicas=len(pod_specs))],
        "replicasets": [fk.replicaset("upf-7c9", "upf", replicas=len(pod_specs))],
        "configmaps": [fk.configmap("upf-config")],
        "secrets": [fk.secret("upf-secret")],
        "pvcs": [fk.pvc("upf-data")],
        "services": [fk.service("upf", selector={"app": "upf"})],
        "pods": pod_specs,
    }


def _upf_pod(name, **kw):
    return fk.pod(
        name,
        node_name=kw.pop("node_name", "worker-1"),
        owner_refs=[fk.owner("upf-7c9", "ReplicaSet")],
        volumes=[fk.cm_volume("upf-config"), fk.secret_volume("upf-secret"),
                 fk.pvc_volume("upf-data")],
        labels={"app": "upf"},
        **kw,
    )


def _build(store, selector=""):
    b = GraphBuilder(_settings(selector), kube_client=fk.FakeKubeClient(store))
    return b.rebuild()


def test_discovers_pods_nodes_and_workload():
    g = _build(_store_upf([_upf_pod("upf-0"), _upf_pod("upf-1", node_name="worker-2")]))
    assert g.node("upf-0") and g.node("upf-0")["kind"] == NodeKind.pod.value
    assert g.node("upf") and g.node("upf")["kind"] == NodeKind.deployment.value
    assert g.node("worker-1")["kind"] == NodeKind.node.value


def test_builds_runs_on_managed_by_and_mounts_edges():
    g = _build(_store_upf([_upf_pod("upf-0")]))
    gg = g.graph
    assert gg.has_edge("upf-0", "worker-1", key=EdgeKind.runs_on.value)
    assert gg.has_edge("upf-0", "upf-7c9", key=EdgeKind.managed_by.value)
    assert gg.has_edge("upf-7c9", "upf", key=EdgeKind.managed_by.value)
    assert gg.has_edge("upf-0", "configmap/upf-config", key=EdgeKind.mounts.value)
    assert gg.has_edge("upf-0", "secret/upf-secret", key=EdgeKind.mounts.value)
    assert gg.has_edge("upf-0", "pvc/upf-data", key=EdgeKind.mounts.value)


def test_service_selects_pods():
    g = _build(_store_upf([_upf_pod("upf-0")]))
    assert g.graph.has_edge("service/upf", "upf-0", key=EdgeKind.selects.value)


def test_health_rollup_all_healthy():
    g = _build(_store_upf([_upf_pod("upf-0"), _upf_pod("upf-1")]))
    assert g.node("upf")["health"] == Health.healthy.value


def test_health_rollup_degraded_when_one_pod_oomkilled():
    g = _build(_store_upf([
        _upf_pod("upf-0"),
        _upf_pod("upf-1", oomkilled=True, healthy=False),
        _upf_pod("upf-2"),
    ]))
    # 2 of 3 ready -> degraded (replicas absorbing the loss)
    assert g.node("upf")["health"] == Health.degraded.value
    assert g.node("upf-1")["health_reason"] == "OOMKilled"
    assert not g.is_healthy("upf-1")


def test_health_rollup_down_when_all_pods_unhealthy():
    g = _build(_store_upf([
        _upf_pod("upf-0", oomkilled=True, healthy=False),
        _upf_pod("upf-1", waiting_reason="CrashLoopBackOff", healthy=False),
    ]))
    assert g.node("upf")["health"] == Health.down.value


def test_empty_selector_scopes_whole_namespace():
    # Two different apps in the namespace; empty selector keeps both.
    store = _store_upf([_upf_pod("upf-0")])
    store["pods"].append(fk.pod("amf-0", node_name="worker-1", labels={"app": "amf"}))
    g = _build(store, selector="")
    assert g.node("upf-0") and g.node("amf-0")


def test_label_selector_narrows_to_one_app():
    store = _store_upf([_upf_pod("upf-0")])
    store["pods"].append(fk.pod("amf-0", node_name="worker-1", labels={"app": "amf"}))
    g = _build(store, selector="app=upf")
    assert g.node("upf-0")
    assert g.node("amf-0") is None  # filtered out by the selector

def test_label_selector_narrows_to_one_app():
    store = _store_upf([_upf_pod("upf-0")])
    store["pods"].append(fk.pod("amf-0", node_name="worker-1", labels={"app": "amf"}))
    g = _build(store, selector="app=upf")
    assert g.node("upf-0")
    assert g.node("amf-0") is None  # filtered out by the selector


def test_safe_list_paginates_via_continue_and_forwards_timeout():
    """Large-namespace lists are chunked server-side via limit/_continue and
    bounded by a per-request timeout, so one unbounded list cannot hang."""
    from types import SimpleNamespace as NS

    from rca_agent.graph import builder as B

    pages = {
        None: NS(items=[NS(name="a"), NS(name="b")], metadata=NS(_continue="t1")),
        "t1": NS(items=[NS(name="c")], metadata=NS(_continue=None)),
    }
    seen = []

    def paging_list(**kw):
        seen.append(kw)
        return pages[kw.get("_continue")]

    items = B._safe_list(paging_list, "things")
    assert [i.name for i in items] == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert all(c.get("limit") == B._LIST_PAGE_SIZE for c in seen)
    assert all(c.get("_request_timeout") == B._LIST_REQUEST_TIMEOUT for c in seen)


def test_safe_list_falls_back_when_call_rejects_kwargs():
    """A simple callable that doesn't accept pagination kwargs still works."""
    from types import SimpleNamespace as NS

    from rca_agent.graph import builder as B

    def strict(**kw):
        if kw:
            raise TypeError("no kwargs")
        return NS(items=[NS(name="x")], metadata=None)

    items = B._safe_list(strict, "strict")
    assert [i.name for i in items] == ["x"]


def test_403_on_a_resource_is_non_fatal():
    """A 403 listing one resource type (e.g. cluster-scoped nodes) must not
    blank the whole graph — the rest of the build proceeds."""
    store = _store_upf([_upf_pod("upf-0")])
    client = fk.FakeKubeClient(store)

    class _ApiErr(Exception):
        status = 403
        reason = "Forbidden"

    def _boom(*a, **k):
        raise _ApiErr()

    client.core.list_node = _boom  # forbidden, like a namespace-scoped token

    b = GraphBuilder(_settings(), kube_client=client)
    g = b.rebuild()
    assert g.stats()["nodes"] > 0  # pods/workloads still discovered
    assert g.node("upf-0") is not None

def test_startup_does_not_block_on_graph_build(monkeypatch):
    """The initial graph build must run in the background, not block startup.

    A large-namespace cluster build can be slow; if it ran synchronously in the
    lifespan before ``yield``, uvicorn would not accept connections (and
    ``/healthz`` would hang / connection-refused) until it finished. We simulate
    a slow rebuild and assert ``/healthz`` responds immediately while the build
    is still running in the background.
    """
    import threading
    import time

    import rca_agent.webhook.app as appmod  # noqa: PLC0415
    assert hasattr(appmod, "_graph_builder"), "expected the module, not the app object"
    done = threading.Event()
    original = appmod._graph_builder.rebuild

    def slow_rebuild():
        started.set()
        time.sleep(1.5)
        done.set()
        return original()

    monkeypatch.setattr(appmod._graph_builder, "rebuild", slow_rebuild)

    t0 = time.time()
    with TestClient(appmod.app) as local_client:  # triggers lifespan startup
        latency = time.time() - t0
        r = local_client.get("/healthz")
        assert r.status_code == 200
        assert latency < 1.0, f"startup blocked on the graph build ({latency:.2f}s)"
        assert started.is_set(), "background build should have started"
        assert not done.is_set(), "build should still be running (non-blocking)"
