#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# deploy-cobra.sh — load & run the read-only rca-agent on the Cobra jumpserver.
#
# Run this ON the Cobra jumpserver (s7427-Cobra-JS, 10.242.70.7) as user eagamil
# (uid/gid 1744, member of the docker group), AFTER running `oc login` so that
# ~/.kube/config holds a valid token kubeconfig.
#
# READ-ONLY by construction: the agent only ever does get/list/watch. It never
# mutates the cluster.
#
# Usage:
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh                 # verify checksum, load image, (re)start, then tail logs
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh --no-logs       # same but do not tail logs at the end
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh --skip-verify   # skip sha256 verification (not recommended)
#
# Override any default via environment variable, e.g.:
#   RCA_PORT=8005 ./deploy-cobra.sh
#   RCA_NF_SELECTOR='app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter' ./deploy-cobra.sh
#
set -euo pipefail

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration (override via environment)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
IMAGE_NAME="${IMAGE_NAME:-rca-agent}"
IMAGE_TAG="${IMAGE_TAG:-0.3.1}"
IMAGE_REF="${IMAGE_NAME}:${IMAGE_TAG}"
CONTAINER_NAME="${CONTAINER_NAME:-rca-agent}"

# Default target matches Cobra 2a / cSAEGW-C.
RCA_NAMESPACE="${RCA_NAMESPACE:-plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301}"
RCA_PORT="${RCA_PORT:-8004}"
# Empty selector = whole namespace. Narrow to one component to shrink the graph,
# e.g. RCA_NF_SELECTOR='app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter'
RCA_NF_SELECTOR="${RCA_NF_SELECTOR:-}"
RCA_REASONING_MODE="${RCA_REASONING_MODE:-extractive}"

# uid:gid the container runs as. Must match the owner of ~/.kube/config (mode
# 600) so the mounted kubeconfig is readable. On Cobra that is 1744:1744.
RUN_UID_GID="${RUN_UID_GID:-1744:1744}"

# Path to the kubeconfig written by `oc login` on the jumpserver.
KUBECONFIG_HOST="${KUBECONFIG_HOST:-$HOME/.kube/config}"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
IMAGE_TARBALL="${IMAGE_TARBALL:-$SCRIPT_DIR/rca-agent-${IMAGE_TAG}.tar.gz}"
SHA_FILE="${SHA_FILE:-${IMAGE_TARBALL}.sha256}"

SKIP_VERIFY=0
TAIL_LOGS=1
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --skip-verify) SKIP_VERIFY=1 ;;
    --no-logs)     TAIL_LOGS=0 ;;
    -h|--help)     grep '^#' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "WARN: unknown arg '$arg' (ignored)" >&2 ;;
  esac
done

log() { printf '\033[1;34m[deploy]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
err() { printf '\033[1;31m[error]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die() { err "$*"; exit 1; }

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pre-flight checks
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "docker not found on PATH."
docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "cannot talk to the docker daemon (is '$USER' in the docker group?)."
[ -f "$IMAGE_TARBALL" ] || die "image tarball not found: $IMAGE_TARBALL"
[ -f "$KUBECONFIG_HOST" ] || die "kubeconfig not found at $KUBECONFIG_HOST. Run 'oc login <api> -u <user> -p <pass> --insecure-skip-tls-verify' first."

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Verify checksum
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$SKIP_VERIFY" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ -f "$SHA_FILE" ]; then
    log "verifying sha256 of $(basename "$IMAGE_TARBALL") ..."
    ( cd "$(dirname "$IMAGE_TARBALL")" && sha256sum -c "$(basename "$SHA_FILE")" ) \
      || die "checksum verification FAILED — tarball corrupt/truncated. Re-copy it."
    log "checksum OK."
  else
    err "no .sha256 sidecar found ($SHA_FILE); skipping verification."
  fi
else
  log "checksum verification skipped (--skip-verify)."
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load the image
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "loading image $IMAGE_REF from $(basename "$IMAGE_TARBALL") ..."
docker load -i "$IMAGE_TARBALL"
docker image inspect "$IMAGE_REF" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || die "image $IMAGE_REF not present after load (tarball tag mismatch?)."

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. (Re)start the container
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "removing any existing container named '$CONTAINER_NAME' ..."
docker rm -f "$CONTAINER_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

log "starting $CONTAINER_NAME (ns=$RCA_NAMESPACE port=$RCA_PORT user=$RUN_UID_GID selector='${RCA_NF_SELECTOR:-<whole-namespace>}') ..."
# Flag notes (from earlier sessions):
#   --network host  : so the OpenShift API server URL resolves/reaches from inside.
#   --user 1744:1744: so the mounted (mode 600) kubeconfig is readable.
#   -e HOME=/tmp    : uid 1744 has no home inside the image; give it a writable one.
#   -v ...:ro       : kubeconfig mounted read-only.
docker run -d \
  --name "$CONTAINER_NAME" \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --network host \
  --user "$RUN_UID_GID" \
  -e RCA_CLUSTER_ENABLED=true \
  -e RCA_KUBECONFIG_MODE=local \
  -e RCA_NAMESPACE="$RCA_NAMESPACE" \
  -e RCA_NF_SELECTOR="$RCA_NF_SELECTOR" \
  -e RCA_REASONING_MODE="$RCA_REASONING_MODE" \
  -e RCA_PORT="$RCA_PORT" \
  -e KUBECONFIG=/kube/config \
  -e HOME=/tmp \
  -v "$KUBECONFIG_HOST":/kube/config:ro \
  "$IMAGE_REF"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Health check — serves immediately now (build runs in the background)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "waiting for the agent to answer /healthz on port $RCA_PORT ..."
ok=0
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do
  if curl -fsS "http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/healthz" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok=1; break; fi
  sleep 1
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# deploy-cobra.sh — load & run the read-only rca-agent on the Cobra jumpserver.
#
# Run this ON the Cobra jumpserver (s7427-Cobra-JS, 10.242.70.7) as user eagamil
# (uid/gid 1744, member of the docker group), AFTER running `oc login` so that
# ~/.kube/config holds a valid token kubeconfig.
#
# READ-ONLY by construction: the agent only ever does get/list/watch. It never
# mutates the cluster.
#
# Usage:
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh                 # verify checksum, load image, (re)start, then tail logs
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh --no-logs       # same but do not tail logs at the end
#   ./deploy-cobra.sh --skip-verify   # skip sha256 verification (not recommended)
#
# Override any default via environment variable, e.g.:
#   RCA_PORT=8005 ./deploy-cobra.sh
#   RCA_NF_SELECTOR='app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter' ./deploy-cobra.sh
#
set -euo pipefail

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration (override via environment)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
IMAGE_NAME="${IMAGE_NAME:-rca-agent}"
IMAGE_TAG="${IMAGE_TAG:-0.3.1}"
IMAGE_REF="${IMAGE_NAME}:${IMAGE_TAG}"
CONTAINER_NAME="${CONTAINER_NAME:-rca-agent}"

# Default target matches Cobra 2a / cSAEGW-C.
RCA_NAMESPACE="${RCA_NAMESPACE:-plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301}"
RCA_PORT="${RCA_PORT:-8004}"
# Empty selector = whole namespace. Narrow to one component to shrink the graph,
# e.g. RCA_NF_SELECTOR='app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter'
RCA_NF_SELECTOR="${RCA_NF_SELECTOR:-}"
RCA_REASONING_MODE="${RCA_REASONING_MODE:-extractive}"

# uid:gid the container runs as. Must match the owner of ~/.kube/config (mode
# 600) so the mounted kubeconfig is readable. On Cobra that is 1744:1744.
RUN_UID_GID="${RUN_UID_GID:-1744:1744}"

# Path to the kubeconfig written by `oc login` on the jumpserver.
KUBECONFIG_HOST="${KUBECONFIG_HOST:-$HOME/.kube/config}"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
IMAGE_TARBALL="${IMAGE_TARBALL:-$SCRIPT_DIR/rca-agent-${IMAGE_TAG}.tar.gz}"
SHA_FILE="${SHA_FILE:-${IMAGE_TARBALL}.sha256}"

SKIP_VERIFY=0
TAIL_LOGS=1
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --skip-verify) SKIP_VERIFY=1 ;;
    --no-logs)     TAIL_LOGS=0 ;;
    -h|--help)     grep '^#' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "WARN: unknown arg '$arg' (ignored)" >&2 ;;
  esac
done

log() { printf '\033[1;34m[deploy]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
err() { printf '\033[1;31m[error]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die() { err "$*"; exit 1; }

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pre-flight checks
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "docker not found on PATH."
docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "cannot talk to the docker daemon (is '$USER' in the docker group?)."
[ -f "$IMAGE_TARBALL" ] || die "image tarball not found: $IMAGE_TARBALL"
[ -f "$KUBECONFIG_HOST" ] || die "kubeconfig not found at $KUBECONFIG_HOST. Run 'oc login <api> -u <user> -p <pass> --insecure-skip-tls-verify' first."

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Verify checksum
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$SKIP_VERIFY" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ -f "$SHA_FILE" ]; then
    log "verifying sha256 of $(basename "$IMAGE_TARBALL") ..."
    ( cd "$(dirname "$IMAGE_TARBALL")" && sha256sum -c "$(basename "$SHA_FILE")" ) \
      || die "checksum verification FAILED — tarball corrupt/truncated. Re-copy it."
    log "checksum OK."
  else
    err "no .sha256 sidecar found ($SHA_FILE); skipping verification."
  fi
else
  log "checksum verification skipped (--skip-verify)."
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load the image
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "loading image $IMAGE_REF from $(basename "$IMAGE_TARBALL") ..."
docker load -i "$IMAGE_TARBALL"
docker image inspect "$IMAGE_REF" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || die "image $IMAGE_REF not present after load (tarball tag mismatch?)."

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. (Re)start the container
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "removing any existing container named '$CONTAINER_NAME' ..."
docker rm -f "$CONTAINER_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

log "starting $CONTAINER_NAME (ns=$RCA_NAMESPACE port=$RCA_PORT user=$RUN_UID_GID selector='${RCA_NF_SELECTOR:-<whole-namespace>}') ..."
# Flag notes (from earlier sessions):
#   --network host  : so the OpenShift API server URL resolves/reaches from inside.
#   --user 1744:1744: so the mounted (mode 600) kubeconfig is readable.
#   -e HOME=/tmp    : uid 1744 has no home inside the image; give it a writable one.
#   -v ...:ro       : kubeconfig mounted read-only.
docker run -d \
  --name "$CONTAINER_NAME" \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --network host \
  --user "$RUN_UID_GID" \
  -e RCA_CLUSTER_ENABLED=true \
  -e RCA_KUBECONFIG_MODE=local \
  -e RCA_NAMESPACE="$RCA_NAMESPACE" \
  -e RCA_NF_SELECTOR="$RCA_NF_SELECTOR" \
  -e RCA_REASONING_MODE="$RCA_REASONING_MODE" \
  -e RCA_PORT="$RCA_PORT" \
  -e KUBECONFIG=/kube/config \
  -e HOME=/tmp \
  -v "$KUBECONFIG_HOST":/kube/config:ro \
  "$IMAGE_REF"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Health check — serves immediately now (build runs in the background)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "waiting for the agent to answer /healthz on port $RCA_PORT ..."
ok=0
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do
  if curl -fsS "http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/healthz" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok=1; break; fi
  sleep 1
done

if [ "$ok" -eq 1 ]; then
  log "healthy: $(curl -fsS "http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/healthz")"
  log "the dependency graph builds in the background; /graph/stats node count"
  log "will rise from 0 to the full namespace within a minute. Current:"
  log "  $(curl -fsS "http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/stats" 2>/dev/null || echo '(starting)')"
  cat <<EOF

  ✅ rca-agent ${IMAGE_TAG} is running.

  View from your LAPTOP via an SSH tunnel:
      ssh -L ${RCA_PORT}:localhost:${RCA_PORT} eagamil@10.242.70.7
  then open:
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/view                 (full graph; orphans hidden)
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/pods                 (pod list: id, health, component)
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/view/<pod>?radius=2  (neighborhood of a pod)
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/graph/stats
      http://localhost:${RCA_PORT}/docs                        (OpenAPI)

  Manage:
      docker logs -f ${CONTAINER_NAME}
      docker rm -f ${CONTAINER_NAME}

  Tip: a 1485-object namespace is a lot to render. To scope to one component:
      RCA_NF_SELECTOR='app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter' ./deploy-cobra.sh
EOF
else
  err "agent did not become healthy on port ${RCA_PORT}. Recent logs:"
  docker logs --tail 40 "$CONTAINER_NAME" || true
  die "startup health check failed."
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Tail logs (optional)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$TAIL_LOGS" -eq 1 ]; then
  log "tailing logs (Ctrl-C to detach; container keeps running) ..."
  docker logs -f "$CONTAINER_NAME"
fi

input.content:
# rca-agent 0.3.1 — Cobra deployment package

Read-only Kubernetes fault-detection & root-cause agent, packaged to run as a
Docker container on the **Cobra jumpserver** against the **Cobra 2a** OpenShift
cluster. The agent only ever does `get`/`list`/`watch` — it never mutates the
cluster.

## What changed in 0.3.1 (why 0.3.0 appeared to "hang")

0.3.0 built the full dependency graph **synchronously at startup**. Against this
namespace (~1485 objects) that first build is slow, so uvicorn never got to bind
its socket — `/healthz` returned *connection refused* (`curl exit 7`) and the log
stalled after `skipping daemonsets ...`. The container was *Up* but not serving.
(The graph-build code itself was byte-identical to 0.2.0; the blocking startup was
the real problem.)

0.3.1 fixes this:

- **Non-blocking startup** — the first graph build runs in a background thread.
  `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/graph/view` answer immediately; the graph fills in
  within ~a minute. (Verified: `/healthz` responds in 0.03s while the build runs.)
- **Bounded cluster list calls** — every `list_*` is now paginated server-side
  (`limit=500` + `_continue`) with a per-request timeout `(5s connect, 30s read)`,
  so a large namespace can't hang or balloon memory on one unbounded list.

> The `skipping nodes: cannot list (403 Forbidden)` / `skipping daemonsets ...`
> lines are **expected and harmless**: the `eagamil` token is namespace-scoped, so
> cluster-scoped `nodes` and some types 403. A single 403 is logged and skipped —
> the rest of the graph still builds.

## Package contents

```
cobra-package-0.3.1/
  rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz          # Docker image (gzipped docker save), ~92 MB
  rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz.sha256   # checksum sidecar
  deploy-cobra.sh                 # load + run + health-check on the jumpserver
  DEPLOY-STEPS.md                 # this document
```

- Image: `rca-agent:0.3.1`
- sha256: `22e182b11642dcaf42ee089c6f3be0c9a7d4e9a1ba158f520d750ca0613d6b94`

## Target environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Jumpserver | `s7427-Cobra-JS` = `10.242.70.7`, user `eagamil` (uid/gid 1744, in docker group), RHEL 8.8, has docker |
| OpenShift  | Cobra 2a — `https://api.cobra-2a-openshift.bete.ericy.com:6443` |
| Namespace  | `plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301` (cSAEGW-C) |
| Port       | `8004` |

## Deployment steps

### 1. Copy the package to the jumpserver (from your laptop/build host)

```bash
scp rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz.sha256 deploy-cobra.sh \
    eagamil@10.242.70.7:~/
```

### 2. Log in to OpenShift on the jumpserver

This writes a short-lived token kubeconfig to `~/.kube/config` (mode 600).

```bash
ssh eagamil@10.242.70.7
oc login https://api.cobra-2a-openshift.bete.ericy.com:6443 \
   -u eagamil -p <password> --insecure-skip-tls-verify
```

> The `oc login` token expires (~24h). If the agent later logs auth errors,
> re-run `oc login` and `docker restart rca-agent`.

### 3. Run the deploy script

```bash
chmod +x deploy-cobra.sh
./deploy-cobra.sh
```

It verifies the checksum, `docker load`s the image, (re)starts the container, and
waits for `/healthz`. Expected log sequence (note startup completes *before* the
build finishes):

```
INFO: rca-agent starting: mode=extractive cluster=True (initial graph build running in background)
INFO: Application startup complete.
INFO: Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8004
... skipping nodes: cannot list (403 Forbidden)        # harmless
INFO: rca-agent initial graph built: {'nodes': 1485, 'edges': ..., ...}
```

#### Manual run (equivalent one-liner, if you prefer not to use the script)

```bash
docker rm -f rca-agent
docker load -i ~/rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz
docker run -d --name rca-agent --restart unless-stopped --network host --user 1744:1744 -e RCA_CLUSTER_ENABLED=true -e RCA_KUBECONFIG_MODE=local -e RCA_NAMESPACE=plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 -e KUBECONFIG=/kube/config -e RCA_PORT=8004 -e HOME=/tmp -v ~/.kube/config:/kube/config:ro rca-agent:0.3.1
docker logs -f rca-agent
```

> Paste the `docker run` as a **single line** — multi-line pastes get corrupted
> over some SSH sessions.

### 4. View the graph (SSH tunnel from your laptop)

```bash
ssh -L 8004:localhost:8004 eagamil@10.242.70.7
```

Then open in a browser:

| URL | Shows |
|---|---|
| `http://localhost:8004/graph/view` | full dependency graph (edgeless nodes hidden) |
| `http://localhost:8004/graph/pods` | pod list (id, health, component) — JSON |
| `http://localhost:8004/graph/view/<pod>?radius=2` | one pod's neighborhood |
| `http://localhost:8004/graph/stats` | node/edge/change counts |
| `http://localhost:8004/healthz` · `/readyz` | health/readiness |
| `http://localhost:8004/docs` | OpenAPI explorer |

### 5. (Optional) Scope to one component

1485 nodes is a lot to render. Narrow to a single component with a label selector:

```bash
RCA_NF_SELECTOR='app.kubernetes.io/name=eric-pc-sm-diameter' ./deploy-cobra.sh
```

List available components from the jumpserver:

```bash
oc get pods -n plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 \
  -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.labels.app\.kubernetes\.io/name}{"\n"}{end}' \
  | sort -u
```

## Verify / operate

```bash
curl -s localhost:8004/healthz                 # {"status":"ok","version":"0.3.1"}
curl -s localhost:8004/graph/stats             # node count rises as the build runs
docker logs -f rca-agent                       # follow logs
docker restart rca-agent                       # e.g. after re-running oc login
docker rm -f rca-agent                         # stop & remove
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `curl: exit 7` / connection refused right after start | (0.3.0 only) startup blocked on the graph build | fixed in 0.3.1 — `/healthz` serves immediately |
| `skipping nodes/daemonsets: 403 Forbidden` in logs | token is namespace-scoped; cluster-scoped types 403 | expected & harmless; the graph still builds |
| `/graph/stats` shows `nodes: 0` for a few seconds | background build still running | wait ~a minute; it rises to the full namespace |
| `cannot read logs ...` warnings | a pod has no previous/current logs or RBAC on `pods/log` | non-fatal; other evidence still gathered |
| `InsecureRequestWarning` in logs | TLS verify off (from `oc login --insecure-skip-tls-verify`) | harmless |
| kubeconfig not readable in container | kubeconfig is mode 600, container uid mismatched | run as `--user 1744:1744` with `-e HOME=/tmp` (the script does this) |

## Safety

Read-only by construction: only `get`/`list`/`watch` are ever issued; there is no
write/patch/delete capability in the code. The mounted kubeconfig is read-only
(`:ro`). The in-cluster Helm chart (`deploy/helm/`) binds a ClusterRole limited to
`get`/`list`/`watch` for the same guarantee when deployed as a pod.

docker rm -f rca-agent                         # stop & remove
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `curl: exit 7` / connection refused right after start | (0.3.0 only) startup blocked on the graph build | fixed in 0.3.1 — `/healthz` serves immediately |
| `skipping nodes/daemonsets: 403 Forbidden` in logs | token is namespace-scoped; cluster-scoped types 403 | expected & harmless; the graph still builds |
| `/graph/stats` shows `nodes: 0` for a few seconds | background build still running | wait ~a minute; it rises to the full namespace |
| `cannot read logs ...` warnings | a pod has no previous/current logs or RBAC on `pods/log` | non-fatal; other evidence still gathered |
| `InsecureRequestWarning` in logs | TLS verify off (from `oc login --insecure-skip-tls-verify`) | harmless |
| kubeconfig not readable in container | kubeconfig is mode 600, container uid mismatched | run as `--user 1744:1744` with `-e HOME=/tmp` (the script does this) |

## Safety

Read-only by construction: only `get`/`list`/`watch` are ever issued; there is no
write/patch/delete capability in the code. The mounted kubeconfig is read-only
(`:ro`). The in-cluster Helm chart (`deploy/helm/`) binds a ClusterRole limited to
`get`/`list`/`watch` for the same guarantee when deployed as a pod.

Done. Here's what happened and what you now have.

## What was actually wrong

The `403 Forbidden` / `skipping daemonsets` lines were a red herring — those are expected and harmless (your `eagamil` token is namespace-scoped, so cluster-scoped types 403, and the code skips them). I proved this two ways: a diff showed `builder.py`, `kube_client.py`, and `dependency_graph.py` are **byte-identical** between 0.2.0 and 0.3.0, and a local 403-on-nodes build still produced a non-empty graph.

The real blocker, confirmed by your `docker ps` (Up) + `curl exit=7` (connection refused): **0.3.0 built the entire 1485-object graph synchronously at startup**, so uvicorn never bound its socket. The process was alive but not listening, and the log stalled mid-build. This was latent in 0.2.0 too; it just surfaced now.

## The fix (shipped as 0.3.1)

1. **Non-blocking startup** — the first graph build now runs in a background thread. `/healthz` answers in 0.03s while the build runs (verified). The logs now show `Application startup complete` and `Uvicorn running` *before* `initial graph built`.
2. **Bounded list calls** — every `list_*` is paginated server-side (`limit=500` + `_continue`) with a per-request timeout `(5s, 30s)`, so a big namespace can't hang.

Verified: 38 tests pass (added 4 regression tests), ruff clean, image smoke-tested.

## Your Cobra deployment package

`dist/cobra-package-0.3.1/` (tarball also at `/home/milind/rca-agent-0.3.1.tar.gz`):

Two things stand out, and both are good news for the fix:

1. **The 0.3.1 fix works** — startup completed and uvicorn is serving (`/healthz` is up), and the build failure was caught and retried in the background instead of hanging. That's exactly the new behavior.
2. **This is a different, environmental problem**: `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/kube/config'`. The container (running as uid 1744) can't read the mounted kubeconfig.

Notice the prompt: `milind@E-5CG2310LQ9` — you ran this on the **build host**, not the Cobra jumpserver (`eagamil@s7427-Cobra-JS`). On the build host, `~/.kube/config` belongs to `milind` (uid 1000), but the container runs as `--user 1744:1744`, so uid 1744 is denied. The `--user 1744:1744` value only matches the *jumpserver's* `eagamil`.

Also, even if the permission were fixed, `~/.kube/config` on the build host likely doesn't point at Cobra 2a (no `oc login` there), so the build would still fail.

```

## Option B — run on the build host (E-5CG2310LQ9) for a quick local test

If you deliberately want to test on the build host, fix the two mismatches:

1. Run the container as **your** uid so it can read your kubeconfig. Drop `--user 1744:1744` (use `--user $(id -u):$(id -g)`), **or** make the kubeconfig readable.
2. Make sure your local `~/.kube/config` points at the Cobra cluster (`oc login ...` on this host first), otherwise the build will have nothing to talk to.

```bash
# on E-5CG2310LQ9 — only if this host has oc login to Cobra
docker rm -f rca-agent
docker run -d --name rca-agent --restart unless-stopped --network host \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e RCA_CLUSTER_ENABLED=true -e RCA_KUBECONFIG_MODE=local \
  -e RCA_NAMESPACE=plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 \
  -e KUBECONFIG=/kube/config -e RCA_PORT=8004 -e HOME=/tmp \
  -v ~/.kube/config:/kube/config:ro \

```

The deliberate design here is that the kubeconfig is mounted read-only and the container runs as a non-root uid that must match the file's owner — that's the "kubeconfig is mode 600 → run as the owning uid" gotcha from the earlier working session. On the jumpserver that owner is uid 1744 (`eagamil`); on the build host it's uid 1000 (`milind`).

Which host do you actually want this running on? If it's the jumpserver, use Option A exactly as above. If you were intentionally testing locally and this host has an `oc login` to Cobra, Option B's `--user $(id -u):$(id -g)` will clear the `Permission denied`.

"""LangGraph reasoning flow.

Wires the same deterministic steps as graph nodes, then adds an LLM re-rank /
explain node at the end. If LangGraph (the ``[llm]`` extra) is not installed, or
reasoning_mode != "llm", we transparently fall back to the extractive pipeline
so the service always works.

The LLM is constrained to RANK and EXPLAIN the rule-gathered hypotheses; it is
never given a tool to query the cluster and cannot introduce a cause that lacks
supporting evidence.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from rca_agent.config import Settings, get_settings
from rca_agent.graph.dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from rca_agent.models.alert import Alert
from rca_agent.models.incident import IncidentReport
from rca_agent.reasoning.extractive import ExtractivePipeline


def _langgraph_available() -> bool:
    try:
        import langgraph  # noqa: F401
        return True
    except ImportError:
        return False


class ReasoningFlow:
    """Entry point used by the webhook. Chooses LLM or extractive mode."""

    def __init__(self, settings: Settings | None = None,
                 graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
                 builder=None) -> None:
        self.cfg = settings or get_settings()
        self._extractive = ExtractivePipeline(self.cfg, graph=graph, builder=builder)

    def run(self, alert: Alert) -> IncidentReport:
        report = self._extractive.run(alert)
        if self.cfg.reasoning_mode == "llm" and _langgraph_available():
            report = self._llm_rerank(report)
        return report

    def _llm_rerank(self, report: IncidentReport) -> IncidentReport:
        """Re-rank/explain the extractive hypotheses with an LLM.

        TODO (Phase 2): build a LangGraph StateGraph whose final node calls the
        configured LLM with the structured evidence (untrusted text fenced) and
        asks it to order the existing hypotheses and write the evidence chain in
        prose. Must reject any hypothesis not already present. For now this is a
        pass-through so behavior is identical to extractive mode.
        """
        report.reasoning_mode = "llm (rerank pending Phase 2)"
        return report


def build_langgraph_app(settings: Settings | None = None):
    """Construct the compiled LangGraph app (only when the extra is installed).

    Returns None when LangGraph is unavailable so callers can fall back. The
    ``settings`` argument is reserved for Phase 2 (LLM provider wiring).
    """
    if not _langgraph_available():
        return None  # noqa: RET501 — explicit sentinel; Phase 2 returns a compiled app
    # TODO (Phase 2): assemble StateGraph nodes using `settings`:
    #   triage -> gather -> graph_walk -> change_correlation
    #           -> hypothesize_rank -> llm_explain -> report

"""Input schemas for detection sources: Alertmanager webhooks and K8s events."""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Alert(BaseModel):
    """A single Alertmanager alert (subset of the v4 webhook schema)."""

    status: str = "firing"
    labels: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    annotations: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    starts_at: datetime | None = Field(default=None, alias="startsAt")
    ends_at: datetime | None = Field(default=None, alias="endsAt")
    generator_url: str | None = Field(default=None, alias="generatorURL")
    fingerprint: str | None = None

    model_config = {"populate_by_name": True}

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return self.labels.get("alertname", "UnknownAlert")

    @property
    def namespace(self) -> str | None:
        return self.labels.get("namespace")

    @property
    def target(self) -> str | None:
        """Best-effort affected resource (pod > deployment > service > job)."""
        for key in ("pod", "deployment", "statefulset", "service", "job", "instance"):
            if key in self.labels:
                return self.labels[key]
        return None


class AlertmanagerPayload(BaseModel):
    """Top-level Alertmanager webhook payload (v4)."""

    version: str = "4"
    group_key: str | None = Field(default=None, alias="groupKey")
    status: str = "firing"
    receiver: str | None = None
    group_labels: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict, alias="groupLabels")
    common_labels: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict, alias="commonLabels")
    common_annotations: dict[str, str] = Field(
        default_factory=dict, alias="commonAnnotations"
    )
    external_url: str | None = Field(default=None, alias="externalURL")
    alerts: list[Alert] = Field(default_factory=list)

    model_config = {"populate_by_name": True}


class KubeEvent(BaseModel):
    """A normalized Kubernetes event (CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, etc.)."""

    reason: str
    message: str = ""
    kind: str | None = None  # involved object kind
    name: str | None = None  # involved object name
    namespace: str | None = None
    event_type: str = "Warning"  # Normal | Warning
    first_seen: datetime | None = None
    last_seen: datetime | None = None
    count: int = 1
    raw: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

        "ImagePullBackOff",
        "ErrImagePull",
        "FailedScheduling",
        "Unhealthy",
        "FailedMount",
        "NodeNotReady",
        "Evicted",
    )

    @property
    def is_fault_signal(self) -> bool:
        return self.reason in self.FAULT_REASONS or self.event_type == "Warning"

Now I can give you exact instructions. The way you "test the new tools when you see a pod in trouble" is to **POST an Alertmanager payload naming that pod** to `/webhook/alertmanager`. With `cluster_enabled=true`, the agent then calls the real read-only `KubeQueryTools` to pull that pod's live status, events, logs, and recent config/rollout changes, and returns a ranked root-cause `IncidentReport` with citations.

The resolution logic (from `alert.target`): it picks the resource from labels in order `pod → deployment → statefulset → service → job → instance`. And `KubeQueryTools._resolve_pods` matches that name as an exact pod, a workload prefix (`eric-pc-sm` → `eric-pc-sm-...`), or a substring. So you can point it at a specific broken pod or a whole component.

## How to test against a pod in trouble

First, find a pod that's actually unhealthy on the cluster (run on the jumpserver where `oc` is logged in):

```bash
oc get pods -n plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 \
  --field-selector=status.phase!=Running 2>/dev/null
# or spot restarts/crashloops:
oc get pods -n plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301 \
  -o wide | sort -k4 -nr | head
```

Then POST an alert naming that pod (replace `POD_NAME`). Run this from wherever you can reach port 8004 (the jumpserver itself, or your laptop through the SSH tunnel):

```bash
curl -s -X POST localhost:8004/webhook/alertmanager \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "version": "4",
    "status": "firing",
    "receiver": "rca-agent",
    "alerts": [
      {
        "status": "firing",
        "labels": {
          "alertname": "PodUnhealthy",
          "namespace": "plantx2avzwcspgc-y-oc-consp-301",
          "pod": "POD_NAME",
          "severity": "critical"
        },
        "annotations": { "description": "pod in trouble - investigate" },
        "startsAt": "2026-10-26T23:05:00Z"
      }
    ]
  }' | python3 -m json.tool
```

The response is the `IncidentReport`: `symptom`, ranked `hypotheses`, `blast_radius`, an `evidence` list, and `suggested_next_steps`. Key fields to look at:

- **`hypotheses`** — ranked candidate causes derived from that evidence.

"""The six deterministic reasoning steps.

Each step takes and mutates a :class:`ReasoningState`. They are plain functions
so they can be used both by the extractive pipeline and as LangGraph nodes.

Rules first, LLM second: these steps gather and score evidence deterministically.
The optional LLM step only re-ranks and explains what these produced; it can
never invent a cause that has no gathered evidence.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import timedelta

from rca_agent.graph.dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from rca_agent.models.incident import Citation, Evidence, Hypothesis
from rca_agent.rag.runbook_retriever import RunbookRetriever
from rca_agent.reasoning.state import ReasoningState
from rca_agent.tools.query_tools import QueryTools


def fence(text: str) -> str:
    """Fence untrusted text (logs, alert annotations) as data.

    Prompt-injection defense: a log line may carry injected instructions, so we
    wrap it in explicit data delimiters before it is ever shown to an LLM.
    """
    return f"<<UNTRUSTED_DATA>>{text}<<END_UNTRUSTED_DATA>>"


def triage(state: ReasoningState, cfg) -> ReasoningState:
    """Identify the affected resource and the fault time window from the alert."""
    alert = state.alert
    state.affected_resource = alert.target or state.affected_resource
    end = alert.starts_at or _utcnow()
    state.window_end = end
    state.window_start = end - timedelta(minutes=cfg.change_correlation_window_minutes)
    state.add_evidence(
        Evidence(
            category="event",
            summary=f"Alert '{alert.name}' fired for {state.affected_resource or 'unknown'}",
            resource=state.affected_resource,
            timestamp=alert.starts_at,
            citations=[Citation(kind="event", source=alert.name,
                                detail=alert.annotations.get("description", ""))],
        )
    )
    return state


def gather_evidence(state: ReasoningState, tools: QueryTools, cfg) -> ReasoningState:
    """Collect pod status, recent events, log tail and key metrics."""
    res = state.affected_resource
    if not res:
        return state
    ns = state.namespace

    status = tools.pod_status(res, ns)
    if not status.get("ready", True) or status.get("restart_count", 0) > 0:
        reason = status.get("last_termination_reason") or "not ready"
        state.add_evidence(Evidence(
            category="pod_status",
            summary=f"{res} unhealthy: {reason} (restarts={status.get('restart_count', 0)})",
            resource=res,
            citations=[Citation(kind="event", source=res, detail=reason)],
        ))

    for ev in tools.recent_events(res, ns, since_minutes=30):
        state.add_evidence(Evidence(
            category="event",
            summary=f"{ev.reason}: {ev.message}",
            resource=ev.name,
            timestamp=ev.last_seen,
            citations=[Citation(kind="event", source=ev.name or res, detail=ev.reason,
                                timestamp=ev.last_seen)],
        ))

    log_lines = tools.logs(res, ns, tail_lines=cfg.log_tail_lines)
    err_lines = [ln for ln in log_lines if "error" in ln.lower() or "fatal" in ln.lower()]
    for ln in err_lines[:5]:
        state.add_evidence(Evidence(
            category="log",
            summary=fence(ln),
            resource=res,
            citations=[Citation(kind="log", source=res, detail=ln[:120])],
        ))
    return state


def graph_walk(state: ReasoningState, graph: DependencyGraph) -> ReasoningState:
    """Upstream = candidate causes; downstream = blast radius."""
    res = state.affected_resource
    if not res or not graph.node(res):
        return state
    state.unhealthy_upstream = graph.unhealthy_upstream(res)
    state.blast_radius = graph.downstream(res)
    for up in state.unhealthy_upstream:
        node = graph.node(up) or {}
        state.add_evidence(Evidence(
            category="graph",
            summary=f"Upstream dependency '{up}' is unhealthy "
                    f"({node.get('health_reason', 'unknown')})",
            resource=up,
            citations=[Citation(kind="graph", source=up,
                                detail="upstream of " + res)],
        ))
    if state.blast_radius:

    changes = tools.recent_changes(

    )
    state.changes = changes
    for ch in changes:
        state.add_evidence(Evidence(
            category="change",
            summary=f"Recent {ch.get('type')} on {ch.get('object')}: {ch.get('detail', '')}",
            resource=ch.get("object"),
            citations=[Citation(kind="change", source=str(ch.get("object")),
                                detail=ch.get("detail", ""))],
        ))
    return state


def hypothesize_and_rank(state: ReasoningState) -> ReasoningState:
    """Build candidate causes from gathered evidence and score them.

    Deterministic scoring (no LLM). Each hypothesis must be tied to evidence;
    anything unsupported is never created. Scoring weights:
      +0.45  a fault event (OOMKilled/CrashLoop/etc.) on the resource or upstream
      +0.30  a recent change correlated in time
      +0.20  unhealthy upstream dependency (cascade)
      +0.15  error/fatal log lines
    """
    res = state.affected_resource or "unknown"
    candidates: dict[str, Hypothesis] = {}

    def ensure(key: str, cause: str) -> Hypothesis:
        if key not in candidates:
            candidates[key] = Hypothesis(cause=cause)
        return candidates[key]

    # 1) Fault events (pod_status/event evidence).
    fault_reasons = {"OOMKilled", "CrashLoopBackOff", "ImagePullBackOff",
                     "ErrImagePull", "Evicted"}
    for ev in state.evidence:
        reason = next((r for r in fault_reasons if r in ev.summary), None)
        if reason:
            h = ensure(f"fault:{ev.resource}:{reason}",
                       f"{ev.resource} {reason}")
            h.confidence += 0.45
            h.evidence_chain.append(f"{ev.resource} {reason}")
            h.supporting_evidence.append(ev)
            h.citations.extend(ev.citations)

    # 2) Recent changes correlated in time.
    for ch in state.changes:
        h = ensure(f"change:{ch.get('object')}",
                   f"recent {ch.get('type')} to {ch.get('object')}")
        h.confidence += 0.30
        h.evidence_chain.append(
            f"{ch.get('type')} on {ch.get('object')}: {ch.get('detail', '')}")
        h.citations.append(Citation(kind="change", source=str(ch.get("object")),
                                    detail=ch.get("detail", "")))

    # 3) Unhealthy upstream (cascade causes).
    for up in state.unhealthy_upstream:
        h = ensure(f"upstream:{up}", f"{up} unhealthy (cascades to {res})")
        h.confidence += 0.20
        h.evidence_chain.append(f"{res} errors <- {up} unhealthy")

    # 4) Error logs add weak support to same-resource hypotheses.
    has_error_logs = any(e.category == "log" for e in state.evidence)
    if has_error_logs:
        for h in candidates.values():
            h.confidence += 0.15

    _link_change_to_fault(candidates, state)

    # Clamp and attach the symptom to the head of each chain.
    for h in candidates.values():
        h.confidence = min(h.confidence, 0.99)
        h.evidence_chain.insert(0, f"symptom: {state.alert.name} on {res}")

    state.hypotheses = sorted(candidates.values(),
                              key=lambda x: x.confidence, reverse=True)
    return state


def _link_change_to_fault(candidates: dict, state) -> None:
    """If a change and a fault reference the same object, boost & chain them.

    Models the headline example: ConfigMap memory-limit change -> OOMKilled.
    Heuristic: the top change becomes the tail of the top fault chain and boosts
    its confidence, expressing "fault caused by the recent change".
    """
    fault = next((h for k, h in candidates.items() if k.startswith("fault:")), None)
    change = next((h for k, h in candidates.items() if k.startswith("change:")), None)
    if fault and change:
        fault.evidence_chain.extend(change.evidence_chain)
        fault.confidence = min(fault.confidence + 0.10, 0.99)
        fault.citations.extend(change.citations)


def build_next_steps(state: ReasoningState, retriever: RunbookRetriever,
                     top_k: int) -> ReasoningState:
    """Pull human-facing next steps from runbooks via RAG (recommendations only)."""
    top = state.hypotheses[0] if state.hypotheses else None
    query = top.cause if top else f"{state.alert.name} {state.affected_resource or ''}"
    hits = retriever.retrieve(query, top_k=top_k)
    state.suggested_next_steps = [f"{h.title}: {h.snippet} (see {h.source})" for h in hits]
    return state

    from datetime import datetime, timezone
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc)

Now I can explain precisely. The code confirms:

- **`hypotheses` and `evidence`** are built *only* from live tool output (`pod_status`, `recent_events`, `logs`, `recent_changes`) and the graph. Nothing there is canned. If the cluster is unreachable, these come back **empty**.
- **`suggested_next_steps`** are built by `build_next_steps`, which queries the `StubRunbookRetriever` using the top hypothesis (or, when there are no hypotheses, the alert name + resource) as the search query. The stub keyword-matches against its 3 canned UPF/SMF/ConfigMap runbooks and returns whatever overlaps.

So here's what happened in your run:

**The runbook suggestions are hardcoded demo data — they did NOT come from Cobra.** They're keyword-matched to your alert text (your alert mentioned SMF/UPF/PFCP, or the stub just returned its defaults). The presence of "fake UPF" runbooks does not mean the agent saw a UPF on Cobra. It only means the runbook RAG is still the stub (Phase 2 not built, and no `RCA_RUNBOOK_RAG_URL` configured).

The question that actually matters — did the agent read real Cobra pod data? — is answered by the **`evidence`** and **`hypotheses`** arrays, not `suggested_next_steps`. Given your earlier `Permission denied: /kube/config` → `nodes: 0` empty graph, I strongly suspect those two arrays came back **empty or near-empty**, meaning the agent never reached the cluster. Please paste the full report (especially `evidence` and `hypotheses`), or just:

```bash
# on whichever host runs the container, through the tunnel or locally:
curl -s -X POST localhost:8004/webhook/alertmanager -H 'content-type: application/json' -d @alert.json \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; r=json.load(sys.stdin)["reports"][0]; print("evidence:",len(r["evidence"]),"hypotheses:",len(r["hypotheses"])); print(json.dumps(r["evidence"],indent=2)); print(json.dumps(r["hypotheses"],indent=2))'
```

Two things to fix so you get *real* Cobra RCA instead of stub-flavored output:

1. **Make the cluster reachable** (the root cause from before). Run the container where the kubeconfig is valid and readable by the container's uid:
   - On the **jumpserver** as `eagamil`: `--user 1744:1744` with `~/.kube/config` after `oc login`.
   - On the **build host** as `milind`: `--user $(id -u):$(id -g)` and this host must have `oc login` to Cobra.
   Then `curl localhost:8004/graph/stats` should show ~1485 nodes, not 0. Only then will `evidence`/`hypotheses` reflect real pods.

2. **Set expectations on `suggested_next_steps`**: these will remain the 3 canned runbooks until the Phase-2 `HttpRunbookRetriever` is wired to your doc-intelligence RAG (via `RCA_RUNBOOK_RAG_URL`). They're advisory demo text, not Cobra-derived.

Want me to make the stub runbook behavior less misleading — e.g. have `build_next_steps` return a clear "no runbook source configured (stub)" placeholder and only emit canned runbooks when explicitly in demo mode? That would stop the report from implying a UPF finding that didn't come from the cluster. I can also add the `evidence`/`hypotheses` count to the log line so you can see at a glance whether live evidence was gathered.

This is actually the real thing working. Look at the `evidence` — it came from **live Cobra data**, not stubs:

- `eric-pc-sm-diameter-7bdcb67999-7tcd2 unhealthy: not ready` — real pod status read from the cluster.
- `Unhealthy: Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500` at `2026-10-27T04:12:56Z` — that's a **real Kubernetes event** pulled from the namespace. No stub produces that string. The cluster is reachable now (the kubeconfig fix worked).

So the new `KubeQueryTools` are genuinely querying Cobra. Two real problems with the *quality* of the output, though, and both are legitimate bugs worth fixing:

## Problem 1 — `recent_changes` has no real timestamp filter, so it floods with noise

Every hypothesis is a `configmap_update` with `confidence 0.3` and `"timestamp": null`. Those `*-db-pg-leader` / `sip-tls` configmaps are **not** related to your SMF pod — they're Postgres leader-election and TLS configmaps that get rewritten constantly. They showed up because:

In `recent_changes`, `_last_modified()` falls back to the object's **creation timestamp** when `managedFields[].time` is missing, and the change gets a `null` timestamp in the evidence. So the "15-minute window" filter isn't actually excluding them — anything without a reliable modified-time leaks through, and leader-election configmaps update their managedFields constantly. The result: 7 unrelated configmaps all scored equally at 0.3, burying the real signal.

## Problem 2 — the actual root cause was found but ranked at the bottom

The strongest real evidence is the **readiness probe 500** event. But `hypothesize_and_rank` only creates hypotheses for `fault_reasons = {OOMKilled, CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ErrImagePull, Evicted}` — it does **not** treat `Unhealthy`/readiness-probe-failed as a fault. So no hypothesis was created for "pod failing its readiness probe (HTTP 500)", which is the thing actually wrong. Instead you got seven spurious configmap hypotheses.

Let me confirm these two issues in the code before fixing.

"""Shared state passed between reasoning steps (LangGraph-compatible dict)."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime

from rca_agent.models.alert import Alert
from rca_agent.models.incident import Evidence, Hypothesis


@dataclass
class ReasoningState:
    """Mutable working memory for one incident, threaded through the flow."""

    alert: Alert
    namespace: str
    affected_resource: str | None = None
    window_start: datetime | None = None
    window_end: datetime | None = None

    evidence: list[Evidence] = field(default_factory=list)
    unhealthy_upstream: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    blast_radius: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    changes: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    hypotheses: list[Hypothesis] = field(default_factory=list)
    suggested_next_steps: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def add_evidence(self, ev: Evidence) -> None:
        self.evidence.append(ev)

"""Output schema: the incident report with ranked root-cause hypotheses."""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from enum import Enum
from uuid import uuid4

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Severity(str, Enum):
    critical = "critical"
    warning = "warning"
    info = "info"


class Citation(BaseModel):
    """A pointer to the primary evidence behind a claim."""

    kind: str  # "log" | "event" | "metric" | "runbook" | "graph" | "change"
    source: str  # pod name, PromQL query, runbook page, etc.
    detail: str = ""
    timestamp: datetime | None = None


class Evidence(BaseModel):
    """One structured piece of evidence gathered deterministically."""

    category: str  # "pod_status" | "event" | "log" | "metric" | "change" | "graph"
    summary: str
    resource: str | None = None
    timestamp: datetime | None = None
    citations: list[Citation] = Field(default_factory=list)


class Hypothesis(BaseModel):
    """A candidate root cause with a confidence score and an evidence chain."""

    cause: str
    # Human-readable chain, e.g.
    # "SMF errors <- UPF unreachable <- UPF OOMKilled <- memory limit lowered".
    evidence_chain: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    confidence: float = 0.0  # 0.0 - 1.0
    supporting_evidence: list[Evidence] = Field(default_factory=list)
    citations: list[Citation] = Field(default_factory=list)


class IncidentReport(BaseModel):
    """The agent's complete output for one detected fault."""

    incident_id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: uuid4().hex[:12])
    created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc))

    # Symptom: what fired, where, when.
    symptom: str
    affected_resource: str | None = None
    namespace: str | None = None
    severity: Severity = Severity.warning
    detected_at: datetime | None = None

    # Reasoning outputs.
    hypotheses: list[Hypothesis] = Field(default_factory=list)
    blast_radius: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    evidence: list[Evidence] = Field(default_factory=list)
    suggested_next_steps: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

    # Provenance.
    reasoning_mode: str = "extractive"

    @property
    def top_hypothesis(self) -> Hypothesis | None:
        return self.hypotheses[0] if self.hypotheses else None

    def ranked(self) -> IncidentReport:
        """Return self with hypotheses sorted by confidence (desc)."""
        self.hypotheses.sort(key=lambda h: h.confidence, reverse=True)
        return self

def change_correlation(state: ReasoningState, tools: QueryTools, cfg) -> ReasoningState:
    """List what changed shortly before the symptom — often the cheapest cause."""
    changes = tools.recent_changes(
        state.namespace, since_minutes=cfg.change_correlation_window_minutes
    )
    state.changes = changes
    for ch in changes:
        state.add_evidence(Evidence(
            category="change",
            summary=f"Recent {ch.get('type')} on {ch.get('object')}: {ch.get('detail', '')}",
            resource=ch.get("object"),
            citations=[Citation(kind="change", source=str(ch.get("object")),
                                detail=ch.get("detail", ""))],
        ))
    return state


def hypothesize_and_rank(state: ReasoningState) -> ReasoningState:
    """Build candidate causes from gathered evidence and score them.

    Deterministic scoring (no LLM). Each hypothesis must be tied to evidence;
    anything unsupported is never created. Scoring weights:
      +0.45  a fault event (OOMKilled/CrashLoop/etc.) on the resource or upstream
      +0.30  a recent change correlated in time
      +0.20  unhealthy upstream dependency (cascade)
      +0.15  error/fatal log lines
    """
    res = state.affected_resource or "unknown"
    candidates: dict[str, Hypothesis] = {}

    def ensure(key: str, cause: str) -> Hypothesis:
        if key not in candidates:
            candidates[key] = Hypothesis(cause=cause)
        return candidates[key]

    # 1) Fault events (pod_status/event evidence).
    fault_reasons = {"OOMKilled", "CrashLoopBackOff", "ImagePullBackOff",
                     "ErrImagePull", "Evicted"}
    for ev in state.evidence:
        reason = next((r for r in fault_reasons if r in ev.summary), None)
        if reason:
            h = ensure(f"fault:{ev.resource}:{reason}",
                       f"{ev.resource} {reason}")
            h.confidence += 0.45
            h.evidence_chain.append(f"{ev.resource} {reason}")
            h.supporting_evidence.append(ev)
            h.citations.extend(ev.citations)

    # 2) Recent changes correlated in time.
    for ch in state.changes:
        h = ensure(f"change:{ch.get('object')}",
                   f"recent {ch.get('type')} to {ch.get('object')}")
        h.confidence += 0.30
        h.evidence_chain.append(
            f"{ch.get('type')} on {ch.get('object')}: {ch.get('detail', '')}")
        h.citations.append(Citation(kind="change", source=str(ch.get("object")),
                                    detail=ch.get("detail", "")))

    # 3) Unhealthy upstream (cascade causes).
    for up in state.unhealthy_upstream:
        h = ensure(f"upstream:{up}", f"{up} unhealthy (cascades to {res})")
        h.confidence += 0.20
        h.evidence_chain.append(f"{res} errors <- {up} unhealthy")

    # 4) Error logs add weak support to same-resource hypotheses.
    has_error_logs = any(e.category == "log" for e in state.evidence)
    if has_error_logs:
        for h in candidates.values():
            h.confidence += 0.15

    # Merge change + fault on the same object into a single causal chain.
    _link_change_to_fault(candidates, state)

def _last_modified(obj):
    """Best-effort last-change time: newest managedFields time, else creation.

    A ``kubectl apply`` / edit updates ``managedFields[].time``; that is the most
    reliable "when did this object last change" signal without the audit log.
    """
    meta = getattr(obj, "metadata", None)
    times = []
    for mf in getattr(meta, "managed_fields", None) or []:
        t = _to_dt(getattr(mf, "time", None))
        if t:
            times.append(t)
    if times:
        return max(times)
    return _to_dt(_creation_ts(obj))


def _managed_fields_time(obj):
    """Newest ``managedFields[].time`` ONLY — no creation-time fallback.

    For change-correlation we want the genuine last-edit time. Falling back to
    the creation timestamp (as ``_last_modified`` does) would make long-lived
    objects with no managedFields time look "recently changed" and flood the
    report with irrelevant candidates. Returns None when there is no real edit
    time, so such objects are simply skipped.
    """
    meta = getattr(obj, "metadata", None)
    times = []
    for mf in getattr(meta, "managed_fields", None) or []:
        t = _to_dt(getattr(mf, "time", None))
        if t:
            times.append(t)
    return max(times) if times else None


# Substrings of objects that are HA / control-plane bookkeeping (leader
# election, TLS supervisor state, kvdb replication). These are rewritten
# constantly by operators and are never an application-config root cause, so we
# exclude them from change-correlation to keep the signal clean.
_HA_BOOKKEEPING_MARKERS = (
    "-db-pg-leader",   # Postgres leader-election (eric-*-db-pg-leader)
    "-tls-ha",         # sip-tls HA state
    "-supervisor-ha",  # sip-tls supervisor HA state
    "leader-election",
    "leaderelection",
)


def _is_ha_bookkeeping(name: str) -> bool:
    n = (name or "").lower()
    return any(marker in n for marker in _HA_BOOKKEEPING_MARKERS)

    A ``kubectl apply`` / edit updates ``managedFields[].time``; that is the most
    reliable "when did this object last change" signal without the audit log.
    """
    meta = getattr(obj, "metadata", None)
    times = []
    for mf in getattr(meta, "managed_fields", None) or []:
        t = _to_dt(getattr(mf, "time", None))
        if t:
            times.append(t)
    if times:
        return max(times)
    return _to_dt(_creation_ts(obj))


def _managed_fields_time(obj):
    """Newest ``managedFields[].time`` ONLY — no creation-time fallback.

    For change-correlation we want the genuine last-edit time. Falling back to
    the creation timestamp (as ``_last_modified`` does) would make long-lived
    objects with no managedFields time look "recently changed" and flood the
    report with irrelevant candidates. Returns None when there is no real edit
    time, so such objects are simply skipped.
    """
    meta = getattr(obj, "metadata", None)
    times = []
    for mf in getattr(meta, "managed_fields", None) or []:
        t = _to_dt(getattr(mf, "time", None))
        if t:
            times.append(t)
    return max(times) if times else None

# constantly by operators and are never an application-config root cause, so we
# exclude them from change-correlation to keep the signal clean.

    "-db-pg-leader",   # Postgres leader-election (eric-*-db-pg-leader)
    "-tls-ha",         # sip-tls HA state
    "-supervisor-ha",  # sip-tls supervisor HA state
    "leader-election",
    "leaderelection",
)


def _is_ha_bookkeeping(name: str) -> bool:
    n = (name or "").lower()
    return any(marker in n for marker in _HA_BOOKKEEPING_MARKERS)

def change_correlation(state: ReasoningState, tools: QueryTools, cfg,
                       graph: DependencyGraph | None = None) -> ReasoningState:
    """List what changed shortly before the symptom — often the cheapest cause.

    To avoid flooding the report with unrelated edits, config/secret changes are
    correlated ONLY to objects the affected pod actually mounts (read from the
    graph's ``mounts`` edges). Rollouts/deployment changes that name the affected
    resource are always kept. When the graph has no mount info for the resource
    (e.g. an empty graph), we fall back to keeping all changes so we never hide a
    real signal — but we mark them as uncorrelated so ranking can weight them
    lower.
    """
    changes = tools.recent_changes(
        state.namespace, since_minutes=cfg.change_correlation_window_minutes
    )

    res = state.affected_resource
    mounted = graph.mounted_config(res) if (graph and res) else set()
    have_mount_info = bool(mounted)

    kept: list[dict] = []
    for ch in changes:
        ctype = str(ch.get("type", ""))
        obj = str(ch.get("object", ""))
        if ctype in ("configmap_update", "secret_update"):
            if have_mount_info:
                # Only keep config changes the affected pod actually consumes.
                if obj not in mounted:
                    continue
                ch["correlated"] = True
            else:
                ch["correlated"] = False  # no mount info -> weak correlation
        else:
            # rollout / deployment / scaling: keep, correlate if it names the res.
            ch["correlated"] = bool(res and (obj == res or (res and obj and obj in res)))
        kept.append(ch)

    state.changes = kept
    for ch in kept:
        ts = _to_dt(ch.get("at"))
        state.add_evidence(Evidence(
            category="change",
            summary=f"Recent {ch.get('type')} on {ch.get('object')}: {ch.get('detail', '')}",
            resource=ch.get("object"),
            timestamp=ts,
            citations=[Citation(kind="change", source=str(ch.get("object")),
                                detail=ch.get("detail", ""), timestamp=ts)],
        ))
    return state

        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(s)

def _detect_probe_failure(state) -> tuple | None:
    """Find a readiness/liveness probe failure for the affected resource.

    Returns ``(evidence, detail)`` for the strongest probe-failure signal, or
    None. Two sources count:
      * an ``Unhealthy`` event whose message mentions a readiness/liveness probe
        (the authoritative signal, e.g. "Readiness probe failed ... 500"), or
      * a ``pod_status`` evidence saying the pod is "not ready" with NO terminated
        fault reason (OOMKilled/CrashLoop are handled separately as faults).
    An explicit probe event is preferred over the generic not-ready status.
    """
    res = state.affected_resource
    probe_event = None
    not_ready = None
    for ev in state.evidence:
        s = ev.summary.lower()
        if ev.category == "event" and ("probe failed" in s or (
                "unhealthy" in s and "probe" in s)):
            probe_event = ev
        elif ev.category == "pod_status" and "not ready" in s and not any(
                r.lower() in s for r in (
                    "oomkilled", "crashloopbackoff", "imagepullbackoff",
                    "errimagepull", "evicted")):
            not_ready = ev
    if probe_event is not None:
        # Extract a short human detail from the event summary.
        detail = probe_event.summary.split(":", 1)[-1].strip() or "health probe failing"
        return probe_event, detail
    if not_ready is not None:
        return not_ready, f"{res} not ready (readiness probe failing)"
    return None

def _link_change_to_fault(candidates: dict, state) -> None:
    """If a change and a fault reference the same object, boost & chain them.

    Models the headline example: ConfigMap memory-limit change -> OOMKilled.
    Heuristic: the top change becomes the tail of the top fault chain and boosts
    its confidence, expressing "fault caused by the recent change".
    """
    fault = next((h for k, h in candidates.items() if k.startswith("fault:")), None)
    change = next((h for k, h in candidates.items() if k.startswith("change:")), None)
    if fault and change:
        fault.evidence_chain.extend(change.evidence_chain)
        fault.confidence = min(fault.confidence + 0.10, 0.99)
        fault.citations.extend(change.citations)

def _link_change_to_fault(candidates: dict, state) -> None:
    """If a CORRELATED change and a fault reference the affected pod, chain them.

    Models the headline example: ConfigMap memory-limit change -> OOMKilled.
    Only a change the affected pod actually consumes (correlated=True) is linked
    as a cause; uncorrelated namespace churn is never chained into the fault.
    """
    fault = next((h for k, h in candidates.items()
                  if k.startswith(("fault:", "probe:"))), None)
    correlated_objs = {str(ch.get("object")) for ch in state.changes
                       if ch.get("correlated")}
    change = next((h for k, h in candidates.items()
                   if k.startswith("change:")
                   and k.split("change:", 1)[1] in correlated_objs), None)
    if fault and change:
        fault.evidence_chain.extend(change.evidence_chain)
        fault.confidence = min(fault.confidence + 0.10, 0.99)
        fault.citations.extend(change.citations)

    """Returns no runbook hits — used when no runbook RAG service is configured.

    This keeps the incident report honest: with no runbook source wired, the
    agent must NOT emit canned remediation text (e.g. UPF/SMF runbooks) that

        return []


def get_runbook_retriever(rag_url: str | None) -> RunbookRetriever:
    """Factory: HTTP-backed retriever when a URL is configured, else a neutral
    no-op retriever (so no misleading canned runbooks appear).

    The keyword ``StubRunbookRetriever`` still exists for demos/tests but is no
    longer the default: emitting its canned UPF/SMF runbooks against a real
    cluster implied findings that did not come from the cluster.
    """
    if not rag_url:
        return NullRunbookRetriever()
